They slammed against the thick, calcified bone plating on the wolf’s shoulder and chest, glancing off with a sharp clack and barely drawing a trickle of black blood.
’Their defense is insane...’ Silas analyzed instantly. ’Standard iron weapons aren’t going to cut it against Tier 2 plating.’
"Shields up!
Brace for impact!" Thora yelled, dropping her center of gravity.
Runa and Thora, the two C-Rank Shieldmaidens, slammed their heavy, iron-banded kite shields together, forming an interlocking wall of wood and steel.
They braced their boots against the dirt just as the lead Umbral Wolf slammed into them.
KRA-BANG!
The impact was deafening.
The sheer physical force of the massive beast violently pushed Thora and Runa back three full feet, their boots carving deep trenches into the dirt.
The wood of their shields groaned dangerously, splintering under the wolf’s crushing weight but they held the line.
"Hold them!
Don’t let them break formation!" Brida roared from the trap zone behind them, cheering her sisters on.
"Girls, listen to me!" Silas shouted over the roaring beasts, his eyes tracking the chaotic melee.
"Do not kill them!
Maim them!
Bring them to the absolute brink of death, but leave the killing blows to me!
I cannot risk the system voiding my UP!"
"Understood!" Thora grunted, her muscles bulging as she forcefully shoved her shield upward, throwing the massive wolf off balance.
Runa seized the opening.
She thrust her heavy iron broadsword forward, bypassing the bone armor and driving the blade deep into the soft unarmored flesh of the wolf’s underbelly.
The beast howled in agony, its corrosive blood spraying across the grass.
Runa ripped the blade out, kicking the beast’s leg to shatter its knee, completely crippling it but explicitly stopping before she pierced its heart.
’My turn,’ Silas thought.
He didn’t hold back as he tapped into his Mythic Gold Core.
Instantly, a brilliant, blinding aura of golden mana ignited around his body.
The raw energy flooded his veins, multiplying his strength, speed, and perception tenfold.
Silas exploded forward.
The ground beneath his boots completely shattered, kicking up a massive cloud of black dirt as he moved faster than the human eye could track.
He appeared directly above the crippled Umbral Wolf.
The golden mana wrapped violently around his Tier 1 Silversteel Spirit Sword, forcing the cheap mythril dust inside the blade into overdrive.
"Die..." Silas muttered.
With a brutal, sweeping downward slash, Silas brought the golden-infused blade down.

The strike didn’t just cut; it detonated as the sheer force behind his twenty points of raw Vitality, combined with the explosive golden mana, cleaved straight through the wolf’s thick neck.𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝐰𝚎𝕓𝐧𝚘𝘃𝗲𝐥.𝐜𝚘𝕞
The bone plating shattered like cheap glass.
The wolf’s massive head was completely severed, spinning violently through the air as a geyser of black blood erupted from the stump.
[Ding!
You have slain a Tier 2 Mutated Umbral Wolf.]
[+2 UP acquired.]
[+50 EXP acquired.
5 EXP allocated to Territory.]
Silas didn’t even pause to read the tabs.
The momentum of the fight was completely intoxicating.
To his right, the other four wolves bypassed the Shieldmaidens and lunged.
"My Lord, behind you!" Alys screamed from the backline.
Before Silas could pivot, a blur of silver-green motion intercepted the beasts.
Eluned, despite holding back her massive spells, was still an SSS-Rank Mythic entity.
She stepped into the path of the charging wolves with the casual, graceful elegance of a dancer.
Without drawing a weapon, she simply raised her slender leg and delivered a devastating high-velocity sweeping kick to the side of the closest wolf.
CRACK!
The sound of shattering ribs echoed like a gunshot.
The physical impact was so overwhelmingly powerful that the massive beast was lifted entirely off its feet, sent flying horizontally through the air like a discarded ragdoll.
It crashed violently into the trunk of a twisted ironwood tree, snapping the thick tree in half upon impact.
The wolf collapsed in a broken wheezing heap, completely immobilized but technically still breathing.
Eluned turned her head, offering Silas a pristine flawless smile.
"It is prepped for you, my Lord."
Silas couldn’t help but laugh with the adrenaline pumping through his veins.
"Good work!"
The remaining three wolves, realizing they were severely outmatched, attempted to scatter.
"Don’t let them run!" Silas ordered.
"Not on my watch!" Fenna and Gwyn yelled simultaneously.
The two Archers drew back their bowstrings, predicting the wolves’ movements with terrifying precision and they loosed their arrows.
The iron tips drove deep into the hind legs of two of the fleeing beasts, severing their tendons.
The massive wolves violently tumbled face-first into the dirt, their momentum causing them to roll and crash into the dark grass, completely hobbled.
The final wolf turned, its jaws snapping wildly as it tried to lunge at Gwyn.
Thora intercepted.
The Shieldmaiden stepped forward and slammed the heavy iron rim of her shield directly into the beast’s snout.

The bone-crushing impact disoriented the wolf and Thora spun, using the momentum of her shield bash to drive the pommel of her broadsword into the base of the wolf’s skull, dropping it to the dirt in a daze.
"Lord Graves!
All four are pinned!" Thora yelled, breathing heavily, sweat dripping down her brow.
Silas didn’t waste a single second.
Gripping his glowing, mana-infused sword, he dashed across the battlefield like a golden streak of lightning.
He reached the beast Eluned had kicked into the tree.
He drove his blade straight down through its skull, the golden mana turning the brain to ash.
[+2 UP acquired.]
He pivoted, lunging toward the two wolves the Archers had hobbled.
He executed a flawless, spinning horizontal slash.
The golden blade carved a massive glowing arc through the air, cleanly decapitating both of the struggling beasts in a single fluid motion.
[+2 UP acquired.]
[+2 UP acquired.]
Finally, he stepped up to the massive wolf Thora had dazed.
He reversed his grip on the Silversteel hilt and drove the blade down into the beast’s heart, twisting it savagely until the glowing red eyes completely dimmed.
[+2 UP acquired.]
The battlefield fell completely silent, save for the heavy ragged breathing of the Shieldmaidens and the quiet hissing of the corrosive wolf blood soaking into the black earth.
Silas stood in the center of the carnage with his chest heaving slightly as the golden mana retracted back into his core.
He shook the black blood off his blade with a sharp flick of his wrist.
’This is amazing...’
He looked at his vanguard.
Thora and Runa’s shields were heavily splintered and dented, but they hadn’t broken formation.
The Archers had nailed their targets perfectly...
TThey had just fought five Tier 2 monsters in a completely open field and hadn’t taken a single casualty.
’These monsters are fucking strong man.’
The density of their bone armor and the physical weight behind their attacks were staggering.
If he had been a standard Red Core Lord fighting an entire horde of these things out in the open, he would have been slaughtered in minutes.
His trap strategy was undeniably the right call.
He dismissed the combat adrenaline and focused his mind on his internal interface checking his Absolute Upgrade System balance.
[Current Balance: 10 UP]
A massive, satisfied grin spread across Silas’s face.
He had the UP.
"Brilliant work, all of you..." Silas praised loudly, looking back at the girls.
"You held the line perfectly."
The Shieldmaidens grinned, heavily exhausted but flushed with the pride of victory.
Eluned stepped up beside him, naturally linking her arm through his with a soft affectionate smile.
"Now," Silas murmured, looking down at the chipped slightly damaged Tier 1 Silversteel Spirit Sword in his hand. ’Let’s see what this system can really do.’

chapters.title: Chapter 11: Hug Your Goddess
paragraphs: Silas stood in the dead center of the carnage as the Umbral Basin was deathly quiet once more.
He looked down at the blade of his Tier 1 Silversteel Spirit Sword.

The cheap mythril-dusted metal was already visibly compromised as deep jagged notches lined the cutting edge and a hairline fracture had begun to form near the crossguard after repeatedly slamming into the calcified bone armor of the Mutated Umbral Wolves.

’Durability is already down to 30 over 50...’ Silas thought, his eyes narrowing as he analyzed the severe micro-fractures running up the fuller of the blade. ’If I keep swinging this thing at Tier 2 bone plating tomorrow morning, it’s going to snap in half by the third wave. A Lord without a weapon on the front lines is just a glorified target.’
He shifted his gaze upward, bringing up his internal interface.
[Current Balance: 10 UP]

He had the exact resources he needed for the upgrade but as he looked at the ten exhausted women surrounding him, wiping black blood from their splintering shields and iron armor, hesitation crossed his mind.

’Do I hide the System from them?’ Silas pondered with his blue eyes sweeping over the Shieldmaidens and Archers. ’Back in Valoria City, exposing a unique trait or a golden finger would get you kidnapped, tortured, or dissected by the megacorporations but we aren’t there.’
He looked at the towering Ironwood Palisade at his back, and then out at the terrifying darkness of the Unknown Zone stretching endlessly before them.

’They are my summons. They are bound to this territory by the cosmic laws of the Sovereign Realm... They literally can’t betray me, and even if they wanted to, there’s no one out here to sell my secrets to.’ Silas reasoned. ’More importantly, they don’t know what a ’System’ is. To them, this realm operates on raw mana and divine laws. If I hide my power, I’m just a guy with a sword but if I show them an absolute miracle... they won’t question it. They will just believe I possess the supreme authority of a god.’
Silas made his choice. Morale was the ultimate weapon, and he was about to weaponize their awe.
"Vanguard, look at me," Silas commanded and the ten women immediately snapped to attention.
Even Eluned, who was gracefully wiping a speck of corrosive blood from her flawless cheek, turned her radiant emerald eyes toward him.
Silas held the chipped, damaged Silversteel sword out in front of him with one hand, letting the ambient purple light of the twin moons catch the fractured metal.

"You fought flawlessly... You held the line against Tier 2 beasts without a single casualty..." Silas said. "But your weapons are basic iron and my sword is already chipping. If we fight the dawn wave like this, we will be crushed by sheer numbers."
"We will fight with our bare hands if we must, Lord Graves!" Brida shouted fiercely, slamming her fist against her splintering wooden shield.

"You won’t have to," Silas replied with a small smile touching his lips. "I told you that we are going to build an empire here but an empire isn’t built on cheap iron. It is forged by the authority of a Lord."
Silas focused his mind squarely on the glowing golden tab hovering over the weapon in his vision.
[Upgrade System: Would you like to upgrade Tier 1 Silversteel Spirit Sword to Tier 2 Umbral-Forged Mythril Blade?]
[Cost: 10 UP]
’Accept,’ Silas commanded mentally.
The reaction was instantaneous and overwhelmingly violent.
A pillar of incandescent blinding golden light erupted directly from Silas’s palm, completely engulfing the damaged sword.

The magical pressure of the Absolute Upgrade System descending upon the physical realm caused the air to crackle and pop, kicking up a massive shockwave of displaced wind that forced the vanguard to shield their eyes.
"Gods above!" Tamsin gasped, falling back a step as the golden aura illuminated the entire dark forest, banishing the shadows of the Umbral Basin.
Inside the pillar of light, the cheap steel of the blade was being fundamentally restructured at an atomic level.
Silas watched in sheer fascination as the chipped edges melted away like wax.
The dull silver was rapidly replaced by a hyper-dense pitch-black metallic alloy that seemed to actively absorb the surrounding light.
Veins of glowing, pulsating purple mythril mapped themselves across the dark metal, resembling the terrifying cosmic sky of the Unknown Zone itself.
The crossguard thickened, wrapping into a brutal highly practical handguard, while the grip elongated to allow for perfect, balanced two-handed strikes.
When the golden light finally shattered like glass and faded into the ether, a brand-new weapon rested in Silas’s grip.
It was breathtakingly lethal.
[Item: Umbral-Forged Mythril Blade]
[Weapon Tier]: 2 (Rare)

[Description]: A highly lethal blade forged from hyper-dense Umbral Steel and lined with pure conductive mythril... It passively absorbs ambient dark mana, making it devastatingly effective at slicing through heavy bone and natural armor.
[Durability]: 250 / 250
Silas gripped the heavy leather hilt.

’The weight is perfect... It’s heavier than the Silversteel, but with my 20 Vitality, it feels like an extension of my own arm. The durability jumped from 50 to 250. This thing is an absolute monster.’
He swung the blade to the side to test its balance and the Umbral-Forged edge sliced through the air so cleanly it actually created a high-pitched vacuum crack that echoed off the trees.
The ten women of the vanguard stared at the sword in shock.
They had just watched their Lord rewrite physical matter with a mere thought.
He hadn’t used an anvil... He hadn’t chanted an arcane spell... He had simply commanded the universe to give him a better weapon, and the universe had obeyed.
Silas pointed the glowing purple tip of the Umbral-Forged blade directly at the massive, severed head of the wolf he had killed earlier.
"This is my authority," Silas declared, his voice ringing with absolute finality.

He looked at the awestruck faces of his troops. "If you fight for me, if you hold the line and bring me the kills, I will not let you fight with splintering wood and rusting iron. Get me the kills, and I will turn your wooden shields into indestructible steel. I will forge your arrows into meteors. No one under my command dies a meaningless death. Do you understand me?"
The morale boost was astronomical. The women didn’t just shout; they roared.
"FOR LORD GRAVES!" the Vanguard screamed in unison, thrusting their iron swords and bows into the air, completely intoxicated by the promise of divine power.
Even Eluned looked at him with an expression of such overwhelming, burning devotion that it could have melted the polar ice caps.
’Hook, line, and sinker...’ Silas thought, highly satisfied as he sheathed the massive black blade.
It slid perfectly into his scabbard, though the weapon was now significantly longer than before.
"Tamsin, status on the Kill Zone!" Silas barked, shifting immediately back into commander mode as the girls began packing the corpses inside.
The Huntress snapped a sharp salute.
"The trenches are dug, my Lord. The deadfalls are rigged using the heavy Ironwood logs but the wolves are tough... the spikes will impale them, but it might not kill them instantly."

"It doesn’t need to," Silas said, formulating the final phase of his trap. ’If we just leave them on the spikes, the sheer number of monsters in the dawn wave will eventually crush the traps by using their own dead as a bridge.’
He looked at the Mages.
"Sybil, Oona. Head into the Armored Barracks... In the quartermaster’s corner, there are heavy barrels of military-grade pitch and oil. Roll them out here and douse the trenches. Douse the spikes."
The girls’ eyes lit up as they realized the sheer brutality of his plan.
"You want to cook them inside their armor," Oona said with a wicked smile forming on her face.

"Exactly," Silas nodded. "If we funnel the wave into the oiled trenches, a single elemental spark from you two will ignite the entire perimeter. It will turn the entrance of our territory into a firewall. Now move!"
The vanguard operated like a well-oiled machine.

While Silas and Eluned kept watch at the edge of the Novice Barrier, the Trap Team hauled the heavy barrels of pitch out from the barracks, sloshing the thick highly flammable liquid into the deep trenches and coating the sharpened wooden spikes they had planted in the earth.

Within thirty minutes, the perimeter directly outside the gates had been transformed from a barren patch of black dirt into a terrifying, highly lethal obstacle course designed specifically to cripple and incinerate anything that tried to breach the doors.
"It is done, Lord Graves..." Tamsin reported, wiping sweat and black dirt from her brow.
"Very good... Everyone, let’s go inside." Silas ordered.
He waited until all ten women had crossed the threshold before stepping back into his territory himself.
Brida and Vanya immediately grabbed the heavy iron locking bar and slammed it down across the massive Ironwood gates.
CLANG!

"Vanguard, you are dismissed to the Armored Barracks," Silas addressed his troops. "You all should rest and recover your stamina... Don’t bother posting a watch; the Novice Barrier will protect us until dawn. When the sun comes up, I want everyone armed and on the walls."
"Yes, my Lord!" the women chorused, bowing deeply before heading toward the warm brightly lit barracks.
Silas let out a long exhale as the adrenaline of the hunt finally began to bleed out of his system.
The physical exhaustion of the day was finally catching up to him.
The awakening... the core evolution... building the massive territory... and fighting Tier 2 monsters had taken a massive toll on his mind and body.
"Come on," Silas said softly, turning to Eluned. "Let’s get some rest."
Eluned nodded obediently, staying incredibly close to his side as they walked up the slight incline of the courtyard toward the massive, two-story Reinforced Stone Keep.
Silas pushed the heavy double doors open, and they stepped inside then he paused, blinking in genuine surprise.
He hadn’t actually taken the time to inspect the interior of the Keep when he built it.
Because it was a Tier 2 Construct, he had expected a large singular stone hall with a bed thrown in the corner.
Instead, the interior was massive and highly structured.
The first floor featured a sprawling war room with a heavy table, several branching hallways leading to storage pantries, and what looked like an armory room.
A set of sturdy stone stairs led up to the second floor.

’Damn,’ Silas thought, thoroughly impressed as he looked around. ’The Sovereign really doesn’t hold back on Tier 2 blueprints... There are actual guest quarters, a bathing room, and a massive master suite up there.’
As the heavy wooden doors shut behind them, cutting off the ambient purple light of the twin moons outside, the Keep was plunged into thick heavy shadows.
The simple iron sconces on the walls hadn’t been lit yet.
Silas felt Eluned suddenly stop walking.
He turned around.
The SSS-Rank Goddess, the terrifying mythic entity who had effortlessly shattered the ribs of a massive Umbral Wolf with a single kick, was standing frozen near the entrance.
Her arms were wrapped tightly around herself.
She was visibly trembling with her breath coming out in short shallow gasps as her wide emerald eyes darted around the dark oppressive stone walls of the Keep.

’She’s shivering?’ Silas thought, his brow furrowing in confusion. ’That doesn’t make any sense... The ambient temperature in here is completely stable, and she has 150 Vitality so she doesn’t feel the cold.’
He looked closer.
He didn’t know anything about her backstory but he didn’t need to know the details to recognize the unmistakable look of pure paralyzing trauma.
’It’s the dark..’ Silas realized, his expression softening. ’The enclosed space... She’s terrified of it.’
Silas didn’t say a word. He didn’t tell her to toughen up, he didn’t ask her uncomfortable questions, and he certainly didn’t mock a literal goddess for being afraid of the dark.
He simply walked back over to her, reaching out and gently taking her trembling hand in his. He squeezed it warmly, anchoring her to the present.
Eluned gasped softly with her terrified eyes snapping up to meet his.
"I’ve got you," Silas said, his voice sounding incredibly soft. "You aren’t wherever you were before. You’re here... with me."
Eluned swallowed hard, a single tear slipping down her pale cheek.
"The walls... they are so heavy, my Lord. It feels like the earth is closing in."
"I know," Silas said gently, leading her toward the stairs. "But these walls aren’t a cage... They’re a shield to keep the monsters out and I’m the one holding the key."
He led her up the stone steps to the second floor, pushing open the heavy oak door to the Lord’s master quarters.
The room was spacious, dominated by a massive heavy timber bed piled with thick furs and wool blankets.
A large window overlooked the courtyard, allowing the golden light of the Novice Barrier to filter in, cutting through the suffocating darkness and illuminating the room.
Eluned practically clung to him. Right now, she wasn’t a weapon. She was just a deeply traumatized woman.
Silas guided her to the edge of the large bed.
"Get some sleep," Silas told her, pulling back the thick furs.
Eluned looked at him with panic instantly flaring in her eyes.
Her grip on his hand tightened to the point of pain. "You... you are leaving me? Please, do not leave me alone in here. I will be good. I will be your weapon, just please..."
"Hey, hey," Silas interrupted softly, sitting down on the edge of the bed right beside her.
He pulled his boots off and set his Umbral-Forged blade against the nightstand within arm’s reach. "I’m not going anywhere."
He slid under the heavy blankets, leaning his back against the solid wooden headboard and he opened his arms.
Eluned didn’t hesitate for a fraction of a second. She crawled under the furs, pressing her body flush against his side.
She rested her head entirely on his chest, her silver-green hair spilling over his black hoodie.
The woman wrapped her arms around his waist, holding onto him as if he were a life raft in a violent storm.
Silas wrapped his arm securely around her shoulders, holding her close as he rested his chin lightly on the top of her head.
"You’re safe," Silas whispered into the quiet room.
He pulled up his digital interface with his free hand, checking the countdown.
[Novice Barrier Duration: 10:12:35]
’Ten hours, huh?’ Silas thought, his eyelids suddenly feeling like they were made of lead.
The sheer comfort of the bed combined with the massive adrenaline crash was overwhelming. ’I just need to rest my eyes for a minute... Just a minute...’
Within seconds, Silas’s breathing slowed. His grip on Eluned remained firm and protective, but his mind finally shut down as he fell into a deep heavy sleep.
Eluned, however, remained awake.
She lay there in the quiet room, listening to the steady beating of his heart beneath her ear.
As a Goddess, a former Spirit of the World Tree, she possessed an innate, unavoidable sensitivity to the souls of mortals.
She could naturally read intent, emotional auras, and the darkest desires of anyone she stood near.
It was a blessing and a curse. In the past, she had sensed the greed and betrayal in the hearts of the Elven Overlords long before they chained her.
Now, lying pressed against the chest of a handsome, powerful young Lord in a dark room, she braced herself.
’What intent does he have for me?’
Eluned tentatively opened her spiritual perception, brushing against Silas’s soul and she froze.

There was sexual intent which was natural and she liked it... Her Lord wanted her but it was little compared to the next one she felt; Eluned was instantly engulfed by a massive overwhelming wave of pure protectiveness.
His soul felt like a blazing golden sun, radiating a fierce, stubborn desire to shield his territory, to protect his vanguard, and to keep her safe from the dark.
It was warm... It was genuine... It was a fiercely loyal soul that had clearly suffered in its own past, yet refused to let anyone under its care suffer now.
A furious burning blush completely consumed Eluned’s pale face. The heat spread all the way to the tips of her slightly pointed ears.
Her heart began to race, hammering against her ribs so loudly she was afraid it would wake him.
He didn’t just see her as a tool... He didn’t see her as a toy... He genuinely, deep down in his very core, wanted to protect her.
Eluned tightened her arms around his waist, burying her burning face deeper into his chest as a profound overwhelming sense of love and devotion swelled.

’You reached into the abyss and pulled me out,’ Eluned thought, her emerald eyes glowing softly in the dim light. ’You do not look at me with greed... You look at me with kindness... I swear it upon the fading roots of Yggdrasil... I will protect you forever.’
The hours bled away in peace.
Outside the Keep, the twin moons of the Sovereign Realm finally sank below the jagged horizon.
The Umbral Basin was cast into absolute pitch-black darkness for a fleeting moment before the bruised-purple sky slowly began to lighten with the approaching dawn.
Inside the Tier 2 Armored Barracks, the vanguard began to stir after some more hours.
Tamsin was the first one up, rolling off her cot and stretching her lean muscles.
She walked over to the heavy iron-banded window, peering out at the golden dome of the Novice Barrier that still covered the courtyard.
"Up and at ’em, girls..." Tamsin called out, grabbing her polished recurve bow. "The sun is coming up, I guess? I don’t really know."
Across the room, Brida groaned, sitting up and rubbing the sleep from her eyes.
She reached down, instinctively checking the edge of her iron broadsword.

"I can’t believe we actually slept," Alys muttered, sitting up on her cot and running a hand through her hair. "We’re in the middle of this place surrounded by very strong monsters, and I slept better than I ever did back home."
"That’s because we have a real commander," Vanya chimed in, strapping her leather boots on.
She grinned, tossing a small piece of wood at Alys. "Did you see the way he turned that cheap sword into a powerful blade? The man is a literal god."
Fenna, one of the Archers, let out a soft laugh as she adjusted her tunic.

"A god, maybe. But did you see his face when he was fighting? He didn’t even flinch when that wolf charged him." She leaned back on her cot, a playful smirk crossing her face. "Honestly? Lord Graves is hotter than every other guy in the town I come from. What about you girls?"

Get me the kills, and I will turn your wooden shields into indestructible steel.
I will forge your arrows into meteors.
No one under my command dies a meaningless death.
Do you understand me?"
The morale boost was astronomical.
The women didn’t just shout; they roared.
"FOR LORD GRAVES!" the Vanguard screamed in unison, thrusting their iron swords and bows into the air, completely intoxicated by the promise of divine power.
Even Eluned looked at him with an expression of such overwhelming, burning devotion that it could have melted the polar ice caps.
’Hook, line, and sinker...’ Silas thought, highly satisfied as he sheathed the massive black blade.
It slid perfectly into his scabbard, though the weapon was now significantly longer than before.
"Tamsin, status on the Kill Zone!" Silas barked, shifting immediately back into commander mode as the girls began packing the corpses inside.
The Huntress snapped a sharp salute.
"The trenches are dug, my Lord.
The deadfalls are rigged using the heavy Ironwood logs but the wolves are tough... the spikes will impale them, but it might not kill them instantly."

"It doesn’t need to," Silas said, formulating the final phase of his trap. ’If we just leave them on the spikes, the sheer number of monsters in the dawn wave will eventually crush the traps by using their own dead as a bridge.’
He looked at the Mages.
"Sybil, Oona.
Head into the Armored Barracks...
In the quartermaster’s corner, there are heavy barrels of military-grade pitch and oil.
Roll them out here and douse the trenches.
Douse the spikes."
The girls’ eyes lit up as they realized the sheer brutality of his plan.
"You want to cook them inside their armor," Oona said with a wicked smile forming on her face.
"Exactly," Silas nodded.
"If we funnel the wave into the oiled trenches, a single elemental spark from you two will ignite the entire perimeter.
It will turn the entrance of our territory into a firewall.
Now move!"
The vanguard operated like a well-oiled machine.

While Silas and Eluned kept watch at the edge of the Novice Barrier, the Trap Team hauled the heavy barrels of pitch out from the barracks, sloshing the thick highly flammable liquid into the deep trenches and coating the sharpened wooden spikes they had planted in the earth.

Within thirty minutes, the perimeter directly outside the gates had been transformed from a barren patch of black dirt into a terrifying, highly lethal obstacle course designed specifically to cripple and incinerate anything that tried to breach the doors.
"It is done, Lord Graves..." Tamsin reported, wiping sweat and black dirt from her brow.
"Very good...
Everyone, let’s go inside." Silas ordered.
He waited until all ten women had crossed the threshold before stepping back into his territory himself.
Brida and Vanya immediately grabbed the heavy iron locking bar and slammed it down across the massive Ironwood gates.
CLANG!
"Vanguard, you are dismissed to the Armored Barracks," Silas addressed his troops.
"You all should rest and recover your stamina...
Don’t bother posting a watch; the Novice Barrier will protect us until dawn.
When the sun comes up, I want everyone armed and on the walls."
"Yes, my Lord!" the women chorused, bowing deeply before heading toward the warm brightly lit barracks.
Silas let out a long exhale as the adrenaline of the hunt finally began to bleed out of his system.
The physical exhaustion of the day was finally catching up to him.
The awakening... the core evolution... building the massive territory... and fighting Tier 2 monsters had taken a massive toll on his mind and body.
"Come on," Silas said softly, turning to Eluned.
"Let’s get some rest."
Eluned nodded obediently, staying incredibly close to his side as they walked up the slight incline of the courtyard toward the massive, two-story Reinforced Stone Keep.
Silas pushed the heavy double doors open, and they stepped inside then he paused, blinking in genuine surprise.
He hadn’t actually taken the time to inspect the interior of the Keep when he built it.
Because it was a Tier 2 Construct, he had expected a large singular stone hall with a bed thrown in the corner.
Instead, the interior was massive and highly structured.
The first floor featured a sprawling war room with a heavy table, several branching hallways leading to storage pantries, and what looked like an armory room.
A set of sturdy stone stairs led up to the second floor.
’Damn,’ Silas thought, thoroughly impressed as he looked around. ’The Sovereign really doesn’t hold back on Tier 2 blueprints...
There are actual guest quarters, a bathing room, and a massive master suite up there.’
As the heavy wooden doors shut behind them, cutting off the ambient purple light of the twin moons outside, the Keep was plunged into thick heavy shadows.
The simple iron sconces on the walls hadn’t been lit yet.
Silas felt Eluned suddenly stop walking.
He turned around.
The SSS-Rank Goddess, the terrifying mythic entity who had effortlessly shattered the ribs of a massive Umbral Wolf with a single kick, was standing frozen near the entrance.
Her arms were wrapped tightly around herself.
She was visibly trembling with her breath coming out in short shallow gasps as her wide emerald eyes darted around the dark oppressive stone walls of the Keep.
’She’s shivering?’ Silas thought, his brow furrowing in confusion. ’That doesn’t make any sense...
The ambient temperature in here is completely stable, and she has 150 Vitality so she doesn’t feel the cold.’
He looked closer.
He didn’t know anything about her backstory but he didn’t need to know the details to recognize the unmistakable look of pure paralyzing trauma.
’It’s the dark..’ Silas realized, his expression softening. ’The enclosed space...
She’s terrified of it.’
Silas didn’t say a word.
He didn’t tell her to toughen up, he didn’t ask her uncomfortable questions, and he certainly didn’t mock a literal goddess for being afraid of the dark.
He simply walked back over to her, reaching out and gently taking her trembling hand in his.
He squeezed it warmly, anchoring her to the present.
Eluned gasped softly with her terrified eyes snapping up to meet his.
"I’ve got you," Silas said, his voice sounding incredibly soft.
"You aren’t wherever you were before.
You’re here... with me."
Eluned swallowed hard, a single tear slipping down her pale cheek.
"The walls... they are so heavy, my Lord.
It feels like the earth is closing in."
"I know," Silas said gently, leading her toward the stairs.
"But these walls aren’t a cage...
They’re a shield to keep the monsters out and I’m the one holding the key."
He led her up the stone steps to the second floor, pushing open the heavy oak door to the Lord’s master quarters.
The room was spacious, dominated by a massive heavy timber bed piled with thick furs and wool blankets.
A large window overlooked the courtyard, allowing the golden light of the Novice Barrier to filter in, cutting through the suffocating darkness and illuminating the room.
Eluned practically clung to him.
Right now, she wasn’t a weapon.
She was just a deeply traumatized woman.
Silas guided her to the edge of the large bed.
"Get some sleep," Silas told her, pulling back the thick furs.
Eluned looked at him with panic instantly flaring in her eyes.
Her grip on his hand tightened to the point of pain.
"You... you are leaving me?
Please, do not leave me alone in here.
I will be good.
I will be your weapon, just please..."
"Hey, hey," Silas interrupted softly, sitting down on the edge of the bed right beside her.
He pulled his boots off and set his Umbral-Forged blade against the nightstand within arm’s reach.
"I’m not going anywhere."
He slid under the heavy blankets, leaning his back against the solid wooden headboard and he opened his arms.
Eluned didn’t hesitate for a fraction of a second.
She crawled under the furs, pressing her body flush against his side.
She rested her head entirely on his chest, her silver-green hair spilling over his black hoodie.
The woman wrapped her arms around his waist, holding onto him as if he were a life raft in a violent storm.
Silas wrapped his arm securely around her shoulders, holding her close as he rested his chin lightly on the top of her head.
"You’re safe," Silas whispered into the quiet room.
He pulled up his digital interface with his free hand, checking the countdown.
[Novice Barrier Duration: 10:12:35]
’Ten hours, huh?’ Silas thought, his eyelids suddenly feeling like they were made of lead.
The sheer comfort of the bed combined with the massive adrenaline crash was overwhelming. ’I just need to rest my eyes for a minute...
Just a minute...’
Within seconds, Silas’s breathing slowed.
His grip on Eluned remained firm and protective, but his mind finally shut down as he fell into a deep heavy sleep.
Eluned, however, remained awake.
She lay there in the quiet room, listening to the steady beating of his heart beneath her ear.
As a Goddess, a former Spirit of the World Tree, she possessed an innate, unavoidable sensitivity to the souls of mortals.
She could naturally read intent, emotional auras, and the darkest desires of anyone she stood near.
It was a blessing and a curse.
In the past, she had sensed the greed and betrayal in the hearts of the Elven Overlords long before they chained her.
Now, lying pressed against the chest of a handsome, powerful young Lord in a dark room, she braced herself.
’What intent does he have for me?’
Eluned tentatively opened her spiritual perception, brushing against Silas’s soul and she froze.
There was sexual intent which was natural and she liked it...
Her Lord wanted her but it was little compared to the next one she felt; Eluned was instantly engulfed by a massive overwhelming wave of pure protectiveness.
His soul felt like a blazing golden sun, radiating a fierce, stubborn desire to shield his territory, to protect his vanguard, and to keep her safe from the dark.
It was warm...
It was genuine...
It was a fiercely loyal soul that had clearly suffered in its own past, yet refused to let anyone under its care suffer now.
A furious burning blush completely consumed Eluned’s pale face.
The heat spread all the way to the tips of her slightly pointed ears.
Her heart began to race, hammering against her ribs so loudly she was afraid it would wake him.
He didn’t just see her as a tool...
He didn’t see her as a toy...
He genuinely, deep down in his very core, wanted to protect her.
Eluned tightened her arms around his waist, burying her burning face deeper into his chest as a profound overwhelming sense of love and devotion swelled.
’You reached into the abyss and pulled me out,’ Eluned thought, her emerald eyes glowing softly in the dim light. ’You do not look at me with greed...
You look at me with kindness...
I swear it upon the fading roots of Yggdrasil...
I will protect you forever.’
The hours bled away in peace.
Outside the Keep, the twin moons of the Sovereign Realm finally sank below the jagged horizon.
The Umbral Basin was cast into absolute pitch-black darkness for a fleeting moment before the bruised-purple sky slowly began to lighten with the approaching dawn.
Inside the Tier 2 Armored Barracks, the vanguard began to stir after some more hours.
Tamsin was the first one up, rolling off her cot and stretching her lean muscles.
She walked over to the heavy iron-banded window, peering out at the golden dome of the Novice Barrier that still covered the courtyard.
"Up and at ’em, girls..." Tamsin called out, grabbing her polished recurve bow.
"The sun is coming up, I guess?
I don’t really know."
Across the room, Brida groaned, sitting up and rubbing the sleep from her eyes.
She reached down, instinctively checking the edge of her iron broadsword.
"I can’t believe we actually slept," Alys muttered, sitting up on her cot and running a hand through her hair.
"We’re in the middle of this place surrounded by very strong monsters, and I slept better than I ever did back home."
"That’s because we have a real commander," Vanya chimed in, strapping her leather boots on.
She grinned, tossing a small piece of wood at Alys.
"Did you see the way he turned that cheap sword into a powerful blade?
The man is a literal god."
Fenna, one of the Archers, let out a soft laugh as she adjusted her tunic.
"A god, maybe.
But did you see his face when he was fighting?
He didn’t even flinch when that wolf charged him." She leaned back on her cot, a playful smirk crossing her face.
"Honestly?
Lord Graves is hotter than every other guy in the town I come from.
What about you girls?"

chapters.title: Chapter 12: Calm Before The Storm
paragraphs: "I’m just saying," Alys muttered, pulling a heavy leather strap tight across her iron cuirass. "the man didn’t even flinch when that massive wolf charged him. He is undeniably hot."
"The hottest man I’ve ever laid eyes on, without a doubt..." Vanya agreed immediately, securing her greaves with a sharp nod.
"Aye," Thora chimed in, checking the tension on her bowstring. "With those striking eyes and that jawline? He’s hotter than any man I’ve seen back home, that’s a fact."

"I’m just being practical!" Fenna shot back, though a nervous, flushed smile played on her lips as she slotted iron-tipped arrows into her quiver. "I mean, think about it. If the portal only pulls women... if this whole territory ends up being entirely female... who is going to father the next generation? An empire needs citizens, right?"

"I’m saying," Tamsin, the Wilderness Huntress, interrupted with a wicked, teasing smirk as she checked the edge of her dagger. "that if Lord Graves wants this territory to have a future generation, he’s going to have to personally provide it. I certainly wouldn’t mind... With his strength and bloodline? I’d happily bear his children."
A collective furious blush swept through the barracks.
Even Brida, the hardened Shieldmaiden captain, let out a loud barking laugh that completely drowned out the terrifying roars of the Umbral beasts outside for a fraction of a second.

"Gods above, Tamsin!" Brida cackled, slamming her massive iron-banded shield against her forearm. "The man is going to have to fight a war outside the walls all day, and then fight a war in the barracks all night! Our poor Lord will die of exhaustion before the monsters even touch him!"

"Do you think he and the silver-haired woman are already getting busy?" Sybil whispered with her face completely red as she adjusted her grip on her staff. "She looks at him like she wants to devour him."
The girls erupted into a chorus of nervous blushing laughter with the absurdity of the joke completely dissolving the paralyzing fear of the Unknown Zone.
Suddenly, the sound of footsteps echoed from the stone path outside and the laughter died instantly.
All ten women scrambled, snapping into a rigid military formation with their faces burning completely red as the heavy iron-banded doors swung open.
Silas strode into the room, but his appearance immediately caught them off guard.
He was no longer wearing his simple black hoodie from the slums.
Instead, he was dressed in a stunning, high-tier-looking set of long, flowing combat robes.
The fabric was a deep, rich black lined with elegant silver-green trims that seemed to shimmer with magical energy.
It was entirely Eluned’s doing.
Before leaving the Keep, the Goddess had completely fabricated the magnificent garments out of enchanted grass and ambient mana, claiming her Lord could not step onto a battlefield looking like that.
And right on cue, Eluned stepped into the room, clinging fiercely to his right arm.
The SSS-Rank Goddess looked breathtaking and she pressed her soft curves against his side, practically glaring at the wooden doors of the barracks as if daring any monster to step through them.
Silas blinked, looking at his vanguard.
They were standing perfectly straight, but almost all of them were refusing to make eye contact with their cheeks flushed a deep crimson.
’Did I interrupt something?’ Silas thought, highly confused by their flustered expressions.
He cleared his throat, raising his free hand to gently massage the back of his neck.
A genuinely shy, somewhat apologetic smile broke through his stoic commander facade.

"Morning, girls," Silas greeted smoothly. "I, uh... I have an apology to make. I was so caught up in the excitement of managing the territory and checking the traps that I completely forgot to distribute your breakfast rations. You fought really well, and I left you starving."
The entire vanguard completely short-circuited.

The overwhelming contrast between the terrifying golden-aura warrior who effortlessly cleaved Tier 2 monsters in half and the genuinely sweet, slightly embarrassed man standing before them was too much.
’He’s so cute...’ the ten women thought collectively with their hearts hammering against their ribs.
"We don’t mind at all, Lord Graves!" Brida was the first to speak, her voice slightly higher-pitched than usual. "We are ready to fight on empty stomachs if we must!"

"No one fights on an empty stomach in my territory," Silas replied firmly. "But before we eat, I want to bolster our numbers... I received some new Troop Summoning Cards, and I want to activate them before the barrier drops. Everyone, out to the courtyard."
The women immediately filed out of the Armored Barracks, stepping out into the cold biting air of the Umbral Basin.
The golden dome of the Novice Barrier was still holding strong, casting a shimmering light over the dark stone tiles.
They gathered around the massive stone archway of the Summoning Portal.

"Say," Alys murmured, unable to contain the joke from the barracks as Silas approached the place. "What happens if it’s all women again, my Lord? The territory needs to expand, after all. Are you going to have to get us all pregnant?"
Silas completely froze with his hand hovering over the portal’s interface.
He sweatdropped, looking back at the archer in sheer disbelief. ’Where did that even come from?!’
Before Silas could formulate a response, Eluned’s head snapped up. The Goddess narrowed her emerald eyes, stepping slightly in front of Silas in a highly defensive yet incredibly proud posture.

"They cannot all be women!" Eluned complained, pouting slightly as she looked at Alys but then, a fiercely competitive spark ignited in her eyes. "However... if that were to happen, there is no need to worry. As a divine entity of nature, I possess the ability to supply my Lord with infinite stamina. He will not falter!"
THWACK!
Silas lightly chopped the side of his hand down onto the top of Eluned’s head, completely halting her unhinged rant.
"Ouch..." Eluned squeaked, immediately dropping her divine posture and grabbing her head with both hands, looking up at him with wide teary eyes.
"Enough of that," Silas said, fighting back a massive blush of his own while the mortal girls in the vanguard desperately giggled into their hands. "Let’s just see who we get."
Silas slotted the bundle of cards into the portal’s stone pedestal.
Instantly, the archway roared to life as a blinding pure white light erupted from the center, completely illuminating the dim courtyard and pushing back the oppressive shadows of the early morning.
Silas stepped back, his hand naturally resting on the hilt of his Umbral-Forged Mythril Blade as the light reached its absolute peak.
Through the swirling ether, ten new silhouettes began to solidify.
The light snapped out.
Ten women stumbled out onto the cold stone tiles.
Just like the first batch, they were dressed in basic linen tunics and leather boots, shivering violently as the freezing air of the Unknown Zone hit their lungs.
Panic immediately seized them as they looked past the palisade walls, their eyes widening at the necrotic trees and the terrifying, bruised-purple sky.
Before the panic could fully set in, Eluned simply sighed and let her [Aura of Genesis] bleed out.

The smell of fresh pine washed over the new recruits. Their racing hearts settled and their fear melted away into absolute awe as they looked upon the silver-haired Goddess, and the striking dark-haired Lord she was clinging to.
Silas quickly pulled up his Lord interface, his eyes darting across the floating tabs above their heads to assess his new forces.
[Name]: Hilda
[Class]: Heavy Shieldmaiden
[Rank]: C-Rank
[Name]: Morwen
[Class]: Swift Archer
[Rank]: D-Rank
He scanned the rest.
Astrid, Sigrid, and Eydis were D-Rank Infantry... Ysolde and Maeve were C-Rank Apprentice Mages... It was a solid, highly balanced pull.
But as his eyes landed on the final tab hovering above a deeply shy quiet girl standing at the back of the group and his heart completely skipped a beat.
She had long, dark hair and was clutching her arms nervously, but the magical signature radiating from her was completely different from the others.
[Name]: Rowena
[Class]: Rune Weaver
[Rank]: B-Rank
[Level]: 1

’A B-Rank!’ Silas thought with genuine excitement flaring in his chest. ’A Rune Weaver... That’s an incredibly rare class. They don’t just cast spells; they literally weave mana into physical patterns. They can craft intricate runes on the fly... either burning offensive runes to shred armor or complex defensive runes to create impenetrable barriers. To pull a B-Rank out of standard summoning cards is a miracle.’

"Welcome to the Umbral Basin," Silas called out with his voice instantly capturing the attention of the ten new recruits. "I am Silas Graves, your Lord. The environment is harsh, and the monsters outside those walls are deadly but you are not alone. You stand with the Vanguard."
The new girls quickly fell to one knee, offering their absolute loyalty as they rattled off their names and classes, just as the first group had done.
"Stand up," Silas commanded, looking over his newly expanded army.
Twenty loyal, capable warriors, and an SSS-Rank Goddess. "Head into the Armored Barracks. We have a battle to win, and you need gear and food."
The twenty women filed into the massive stone barracks.
Silas directed the new recruits to the quartermaster’s corner, opening the Standard Weapon Chest.
He handed Hilda and the infantry thick wooden shields and iron broadswords and he gave the new archers their bows.
When Rowena stepped up, Silas handed her a beautifully balanced staff placing it in the woman’s hands.
"Here you go..."
Rowena’s eyes widened in awe, her cheeks flushing as she took the weapon from his hands.
"Y-yes, Lord Graves. Thank you."
With everyone armed, Silas materialized the crates of Military Food Rations into the center of the room.
He leaned back against the solid stone wall, crossing his arms over his chest as the women sat down on the long rows of cots.
"Let me assist you, my Lord," Eluned murmured happily.
The Goddess raised her hand.
Instead of making the girls line up... glowing semi-translucent green roots sprouted effortlessly from the wooden floorboards.
The roots moved with gentle, precise care, picking up the heavy blocks of dried meat and canteens of purified water from the crates and carrying them directly to each of the twenty girls.
The Vanguard watched in sheer amazement as the divine magic catered to them like personal servants.
Eluned, however, saved a single piece of the high-calorie dried meat for herself.
She walked over to where Silas was leaning against the wall and stood incredibly close to him.
With a deeply affectionate smile, she held the piece of food up to his lips.
"Would you like me to feed you my lord?"
Silas could have taken it from her hand, but seeing the genuine devotion in her eyes, he simply smiled and leaned forward, taking a bite directly from her fingers.
Eluned’s breath hitched with her cheeks burning slightly at the intimate contact.
Not wanting to leave her out, Silas reached out, broke off a small piece of the ration, and gently held it to her lips.
"F-for me?"
The Goddess practically melted, closing her eyes as she accepted the food from her Lord, chewing happily.
Across the room, the girls watched the exchange with massive smiles.
"Lord Graves!" Tamsin called out boldly, stepping off her cot with a piece of her own ration. "If you’re accepting offerings, I have a piece of perfectly salted beef right here!"
"Me too!" Fenna chimed in, rushing over with her canteen. "You need to hydrate, my Lord!"
Within seconds, Silas was surrounded by his boldest troops, all playfully offering to feed him or give him water.
Instead of asserting harsh military discipline, Silas just threw his head back and laughed, thoroughly enjoying the wholesome camaraderie.

He accepted a sip of water from Fenna and a piece of meat from Tamsin, cementing their diehard affection for him but the joyful atmosphere was violently shattered by a sound that shook the very dust from the ceiling.
BOOOOOOM.
It sounded like a massive boulder slamming into the golden dome of the Novice Barrier.
The terrified roars of the Umbral beasts outside reached a deafening crescendo.
Silas’s smile vanished.

"Breakfast is over," Silas barked, his voice cracking like a whip. "Helmets on! Archers and Mages, to the high palisade scaffolding! Shieldmaidens and Infantry, form the phalanx behind the gates! Move!"
The twenty women moved like lightning with their previous exhaustion completely erased by the food and the morale boost.
They flooded out of the barracks, taking up their defensive positions.
Silas drew his massive Umbral-Forged Mythril Blade with the purple veins glowing violently as he walked to the very front of the formation.
"Brida! Vanya!" Silas ordered. "Open the gates!"
The two strongest Shieldmaidens heaved the heavy locking bar off the Ironwood Palisade.
The massive doors swung open revealing the absolute nightmare waiting for them.
The golden dome of the Novice Barrier was currently holding back a literal sea of monsters.
There were easily over a hundred Tier 2 beasts churning at the edge of the barrier.
Mutated Umbral Wolves the size of draft horses frothed at the mouth.
Massive, low-slung reptilian creatures covered in jagged stone scales slammed their bodies against the golden light.
Towering, corrupted bears with exposed bone spikes roared in feral madness.
"Gods above..." Rowena, the new B-Rank Rune Weaver whispered.
Silas narrowed his eyes,

He had 20 troops and an oil-flooded trap zone but if he had to run around and manually land the killing blow on over a hundred monsters just to harvest the Upgrade Points, they were going to get overrun.
It was physically impossible to secure every kill in a massive melee.

’System,’ Silas called out in his mind. ’I need an answer right now. If my summoned troops who are bound to my territory and my soul kill a monster without me touching it... do I still receive the UP?’
A pristine glowing tab materialized directly in the center of his vision.

[System Query... Affirmative. All Vassals summoned via the Territory Portal are extensions of the Lord’s Authority. Any kills secured by your troops will deposit Upgrade Points directly into your balance.]
A massive grin spread across Silas’s face.
He didn’t have to hold them back anymore since his army was his weapon.

"Vanguard, listen to me!" Silas roared, raising his black sword high into the air. "You do not hold back! You do not maim! Every single beast that steps past that gate is to be slaughtered! Annihilate them all!"
"YES, LORD GRAVES!" the twenty women screamed in unison, drawing their weapons.
Silas looked up at his digital interface as the blue holographic numbers were aggressively ticking down.
[Novice Barrier Duration: 00:00:05]
The horde of monsters pressed against the barrier with their claws scraping uselessly against the golden light as their jaws snapping in hunger.
Silas lowered his center of gravity, gripping his sword with both hands.
With a sound like a shattering cathedral window, the massive impenetrable golden dome of the Novice Barrier burst into millions of dissipating light particles.
The shield was gone.
For a fraction of a second, the Umbral Basin was completely silent and then, the massive, bone-plated alpha wolf at the front of the pack let out a deafening howl and launched itself forward.
The entire horde charged as the dawn wave had begun.
