"MAGES, NOW!" Silas roared.
Up on the heavy wooden scaffolding built into the palisade walls, Sybil, Oona, Ysolde, and Maeve thrust their iron-shod staves forward.

Channeling every drop of raw mana in their Level 1 bodies, four bright highly concentrated sparks of elemental fire shot from the tips of their foci, streaking through the dim morning air like miniature comets.
The sparks hit the pitch-flooded trenches perfectly.
FWOOM!
The ignition was instantaneous and catastrophic.
A massive, towering wall of roaring orange flames violently erupted from the earth, shooting twenty feet into the bruised-purple sky.
The intense blistering heat washed over the Vanguard forcing Silas to squint against the sudden updraft of scorching wind.
The trap didn’t just slow the horde down; it absolutely broke their momentum.
The leading line of massive Umbral Wolves and stone-scaled reptiles couldn’t stop their charge in time.
They crashed headfirst into the roaring firewall, tumbling violently into the deep trenches.
The sharpened oil-slicked wooden Ironwood spikes impaled them, driving deep into their soft underbellies, while the military-grade pitch clung to their fur and scales like napalm.
The monsters shrieked in absolute blood-curdling agony as they were cooked alive inside their own natural armor.
"Archers, loose!" Tamsin screamed from the frontline.
Thwip!
Thwip!
Thwip!
Thwip!
A massive volley of iron-tipped arrows rained down from Fenna, Alys, Morwen, and the other archers stationed high on the walls.
The projectiles plunged directly into the flames, striking the burning trapped beasts.
Instantly, a cascade of blue holographic tabs began popping up over the girls’ heads, visible only to Silas’s Lord interface.
[Vassal Alys has leveled up! (Level 2)]
[Vassal Sybil has leveled up! (Level 2)]
[Vassal Oona has leveled up! (Level 2)]
"Keep firing!" Silas ordered, but his eyes narrowed.
The horde was simply too massive.
Driven by feral madness, the monsters in the back didn’t stop.
They kept charging, using the burning, screaming bodies of their own packmates as literal bridges to cross the flaming trenches.
A massive, bone-plated wolf cleared the flames with its fur heavily singed and smoking as it landed heavily right in front of the Vanguard’s phalanx.
It let out a deafening roar, raising its massive claws.
"Hold the line!" Brida roared.
KRA-BANG!
The impact was sickening.

The wolf slammed into the interlocking wall of wooden shields held by Brida, Hilda, and Vanya and the sheer physical force pushed the three Shieldmaidens back two full feet with their boots carving deep trenches into the stone courtyard.
Before the beast could snap its jaws, a blur of dark motion intercepted it.
Rowena, the new B-Rank Rune Weaver, stepped out from behind the Shieldmaidens.
Her eyes were glowing with a bright, ethereal blue light as she gripped her staff and swept the tip through the empty air.
A trail of glowing blue mana lingered behind the wood, instantly forming a complex sigil.
"Ignis..." Rowena whispered softly.

The rune detonated as a highly pressurized shockwave of searing arcane heat blasted the wolf point-blank in the chest, shattering its calcified bone plating and sending it tumbling backward into the dirt.
’Her casting speed is insane...’ Silas analyzed, thoroughly impressed by the B-Rank class.
Silas didn’t waste the opening as he tapped into his Mythic Gold Core.
A brilliant blinding aura of golden mana ignited around his body, violently pushing back the heat of the pitch fire.
He gripped the heavy leather hilt of his Tier 2 Umbral-Forged Mythril Blade and exploded forward, moving faster than the human eye could track.
He appeared directly above the stunned wolf.
The Umbral Steel of his black blade actively absorbed the ambient dark mana of the Unknown Zone, turning the edge into a literal void that hungered for destruction.
"Die..." Silas commanded.
With a brutal, sweeping downward slash, Silas brought the golden-infused blade down.
The Tier 2 edge completely bypassed the beast’s natural defenses, cleaving cleanly through its thick neck and splitting its skull in half before burying itself deep into the earth.
[Ding!
Vassal/Lord Kill Registered. +2 UP acquired.]
[+50 EXP acquired.]
[You have Leveled up to Level 3!]
"Push forward!
Do not let them breach the gates!" Silas roared, ripping his blade from the dirt and spinning to meet the next wave of monsters pouring over the fire.
The battlefield descended into absolute brutal chaos.
The trap had successfully neutralized the initial surge, but the sheer numbers meant the fight was devolving into a grueling bloody melee of attrition.
Silas moved like a golden reaper through the thick black smoke and falling ash.
The Vanguard operated with terrifying efficiency.
Every time the Shieldmaidens pinned a beast, or the Archers hobbled a monster with a well-placed volley,
Silas or the Infantry girls were there to secure the kill.
The notifications in Silas’s peripheral vision were going absolutely crazy.
[+2 UP acquired.]
[+2 UP acquired.]
[+2 UP acquired.]
[Vassal Brida has leveled up! (Level 3)]
[Vassal Tamsin has leveled up! (Level 3)]
[Vassal Rowena has leveled up! (Level 2)]
But the physical toll of fighting over a hundred heavily armored Tier 2 Spirit Beasts was beginning to show.
CRACK!
"My shield!" Hilda yelled, gritting her teeth as a massive stone-scaled reptile slammed its heavy tail against her wooden kite shield.
The thick Ironwood completely splintered down the middle with the metal bands popping off under the force of attacks.
To her left, Vanya’s iron broadsword bounced off the skull of a corrupted bear, a massive chip flying off the cheap metal edge.
’The standard gear is reaching its limit...’ Silas thought, deflecting a massive claw strike from a wolf and kicking it backward into the dirt.
He quickly glanced at his internal interface.
[Current Balance: 146 UP]
He had been rapidly accumulating Upgrade Points from the absolute slaughter.
It was time to use them.
"Brida!
Hilda!
Hold your ground!" Silas roared, disengaging from his current target and sprinting toward the crumbling frontline.
He slid to a halt directly behind the Shieldmaidens just as another wave of wolves crashed against them.
Silas reached out, slamming his open palms directly onto the backs of Brida and Hilda’s splintering wooden shields.
’System!
Upgrade!’ Silas commanded mentally.
[Upgrade System: Would you like to upgrade Tier 1 Wooden Kite Shields to Tier 2 Steel Aegis?
Cost: 20 UP]
’Accept!’
A blinding pillar of golden light erupted right in the middle of the blood-soaked battlefield.
The magical pressure of the Absolute Upgrade System descending upon the physical realm caused the air to crackle and pop.
The Umbral Wolves pressing against the shields yelped, violently pushed back by the shockwave of displaced wind.
Before the girls’ very eyes, the splintered, rotting wood of their shields melted away like wax.
In less than a second, the material was fundamentally restructured, rapidly replaced by a hyper-dense gleaming silver-black alloy.
The new shields were thicker, perfectly contoured, and completely impervious to basic physical strikes.
"Gods above..." Brida gasped, feeling the immense, perfectly balanced weight of the Tier 2 Steel in her hand.
"Don’t just stare at it!
Bash them!" Silas barked, moving down the line.
He touched Vanya’s chipped broadsword, triggering another burst of golden light.
[Upgrade System: Tier 1 Iron Broadsword upgraded to Tier 2 Blood-Iron Cleaver.
Cost: 10 UP]
He pointed at the scaffolding above. ’System, range upgrade!’
[Upgrade System: Tier 1 Iron Bows upgraded to Tier 2 Magical Recurve Bows.
Cost: 30 UP]
Up on the walls, Fenna, Alys, and Morwen gasped as their cheap wooden bows suddenly violently restructured into sleek, glowing weapons composed of dark enchanted timber and mythril strings.
When they pulled the strings back, arrows of pure condensed mana automatically formed.
"Holy shit!" Fenna screamed in pure delight.
"Eat this, you ugly bastards!"
She loosed the mana arrow.
It tore through the air with a high-pitched shriek, slamming into a stone-scaled reptile and completely detonating upon impact, blowing a massive hole straight through its torso.
The morale boost was astronomical.
"FOR LORD GRAVES!" the Vanguard roared, completely intoxicated by the sudden surge of power.
With their upgraded Tier 2 gear, the Vanguard was no longer just holding the line; they were actively pushing the horde back.

The Shieldmaidens used their Steel to literally shatter the jaws of the wolves that charged them, while the Infantry stepped in with Blood-Iron Cleavers that sheared through bone plating like hot knives through butter.
But even with upgraded gear, they were still mortal women fighting a literal army.
"Gah!" Tamsin grunted, stumbling backward as a wolf’s corrosive saliva splashed across her iron pauldron with the acid hissing as it ate into the metal and burned her skin.
Across the line, the girls were panting heavily.
The adrenaline was masking their fatigue, but their stamina bars were dropping precariously low.
A few had minor cuts, bruised ribs from the impacts, and their breathing was growing ragged.
Silas parried a strike, severing a wolf’s leg before looking up at the high palisade wall directly behind the gates.𝒻𝘳𝘦𝘦𝘸ℯ𝒷𝘯𝘰𝑣ℯ𝑙.𝘤𝑜𝘮
Eluned was standing there, exactly where he had ordered her to stay.
Her silver-green hair whipped wildly in the wind with her emerald eyes tracking every single movement on the battlefield.
She wasn’t casting offensive spells, respecting Silas’s command to let them harvest the kills, but she was vibrating with anxiousness.
"Eluned!" Silas roared over the din of battle.
"Support!"
The SSS-Rank Goddess’s face instantly lit up with a radiant breathtaking smile.
"With pleasure, my Lord!" Eluned called out, her melodic voice easily cutting through the horrific roars of the monsters.
She gracefully raised both of her hands toward the bruised-purple sky though she didn’t chant but she simply tapped into her divine authority.
"Aura of Genesis: Overgrowth..." she whispered.
Instantly, a massive, pulse-wave of pure, blinding emerald light erupted from her body.

The sheer density of her SSS-Rank mana completely drowned out the dark, necrotic energy of the Umbral Basin as a gentle shimmering green rain began to fall exclusively over Silas and the twenty women of the Vanguard.
The effects were miraculous.
The moment the green light touched Tamsin’s shoulder, the acid burn completely vanished, leaving behind flawless unblemished skin.
Brida’s bruised ribs instantly healed and the heavy suffocating exhaustion plaguing the girls’ muscles evaporated in a fraction of a second.
[System Alert: Aura of Genesis is active.
All Vassals have received ’Absolute Restoration’.
Health is locked at 100%...
Stamina is locked at 100% for the next 10 minutes...]
The girls’ eyes widened in sheer disbelief.
They weren’t just healed; they felt like they could rip a mountain in half with their bare hands.
They possessed infinite stamina.
"They can’t hurt us!" Vanya screamed, laughing maniacally as she charged forward.
"The Goddess protects us!"
Empowered by infinite stamina and wielding Tier 2 magical weapons, the Vanguard turned into an absolute meat grinder.
They abandoned their defensive phalanx and waded directly into the burning trenches, slaughtering the remaining beasts with ruthless efficiency.
Silas stood in the center of the carnage, his chest heaving slightly as he watched his girls completely decimate the surviving monsters.
He pulled up his interface, watching the last of the beasts fall.
’We just killed over a hundred Tier 2 monsters in less than twenty minutes,’ Silas thought with a cold sweat breaking out on his neck as the reality of the Sovereign Realm set in.
He looked at the terrifying environment around him.
’How would a regular Lord survive this?

If I had stayed in my Red Core, if I didn’t have the Absolute Upgrade System to fix their weapons mid-fight, and if I didn’t pull an SSS-Rank Goddess who grants infinite stamina... this dawn wave would have been a literal death sentence.
A standard Lord and ten Level 1 peasants would have been slaughtered in ten seconds.’
The world was cruel and it didn’t care about fairness.
Just as Silas was lowering his blade, thinking the wave was finally broken, a massive glaring red holographic tab suddenly violently expanded in the center of his vision.
[WARNING: MINI-BOSS DETECTED.]
The ground beneath Silas’s boots violently shuddered.
It wasn’t the rolling thunder of a horde this time.
It was the heavy singular earth-shattering footfalls of something massive.
From the absolute darkness of the twisted treeline, the heavy trunks of the Ironwood trees were violently ripped out of the earth by their roots and tossed aside like toothpicks.
Stepping out into the clearing was a nightmare made flesh.
It was a Corrupted Ursine, but it was three times the size of the bears they had just fought.
It stood easily twenty feet tall on its hind legs, its body covered in a sickeningly thick carapace of jagged glowing purple bone armor.
Miasma literally leaked from its jaws, killing the black grass wherever its saliva dropped.
Silas immediately triggered his Lord [Appraisal] skill.
[Monster: Corrupted Ursine Overlord]
[Mini-Boss Rank]: Tier 3
[Description]: An apex predator of the Umbral Basin.
Possesses hyper-dense bone plating that negates low-tier magic and physical strikes.
It is highly aggressive and highly lethal.
The massive Overlord let out a roar so powerful it actually generated a physical shockwave, snuffing out the remaining pitch fires in the trenches.
"Focus fire on the big one!" Tamsin yelled, pulling her bowstring back.
Fenna, Alys, and Morwen unleashed a barrage of mana-arrows from their upgraded bows.
The glowing projectiles slammed directly into the boss’s chest and shattered harmlessly against its thick bone plating, barely leaving a scorch mark.
"It’s too thick!" Fenna shouted in panic.
Rowena stepped forward, her hands glowing with frantic blue light as she rapidly carved a offensive rune into the air.
"Sunder!"
A massive blade of pure arcane energy shot forward, striking the beast directly on the knee.
The rune exploded with tremendous force, kicking up a massive cloud of dust but when the smoke cleared, the Tier 3 Boss hadn’t even flinched.
It slowly turned its glowing, blood-red eyes toward Rowena, dropping to all fours.
"Fall back!" Silas roared, stepping perfectly in front of the Rune Weaver, his golden aura flaring to its absolute maximum.
He gripped his Umbral-Forged blade with both hands.
’I can cut it,’ Silas calculated rapidly. ’My weapon is Tier 2, but with 20 Vitality and my Gold Core, I can crack that armor if I hit the exact same spot multiple times.’
It would be a brutal bloody fight.
"My Lord!"
The melodic, utterly calm voice echoed from above.
Silas glanced up.
Eluned was still standing gracefully on the edge of the high palisade wall.
Her arms were resting politely in front of her as she looked completely bored by the towering, terrifying Tier 3 Boss currently preparing to charge them.
"May I?" Eluned asked politely, tilting her head with a soft smile.
"It is rather loud, and I believe you have gathered enough resources for the morning."
Silas looked at the Goddess, then looked at the twenty exhausted girls standing behind him.
He didn’t need to be a hero right now...
He needed to be a smart Lord...
"Eradicate it, Eluned," Silas commanded.
Eluned’s smile widened into something truly terrifyingly divine.
"As you wish."
She simply raised her right hand, pointing her slender index finger directly at the charging Tier 3 Mini-Boss.
The ambient mana in the entire Umbral Basin violently warped, rushing toward her fingertip in a suffocating vacuum.
The sky physically darkened as a microscopic bead of pure, hyper-compressed SSS-Rank nature mana materialized at the tip of her finger.
"Nature’s Execution..." she whispered.
BOOOOOOOOOOM!
The sound completely shattered the sound barrier.
A blinding, hyper-condensed beam of pure emerald light shot from her finger.
It moved so fast it practically deleted the space between the wall and the boss.
The beam struck the Corrupted Ursine Overlord directly in the chest.
There was no struggle...
There was no resistance...
The Tier 3 bone plating, the massive muscles, and the corrupted flesh simply ceased to exist...

The sheer overwhelming destructive power of the SSS-Rank magic instantly vaporized the entire upper half of the massive beast, turning it into fine dissipating ash before it could even register the pain.
The beam continued straight through the boss, carving a massive smoking trench through the necrotic forest behind it for nearly two miles, completely leveling everything in its path.
The lower half of the boss’s legs stood frozen for a single second, before slowly toppling over into the dirt with a heavy, pathetic thud.
The battlefield fell completely utterly silent.
The remaining monsters lurking in the shadows of the forest took one look at the sheer devastation and immediately turned and fled deeper into the Unknown Zone, completely breaking the dawn wave.
Silas stood frozen, his eyes wide as he stared at the two-mile-long trench carved into the earth.
’...Holy shit.’
Up on the wall, Eluned lowered her hand, brushing a stray lock of silver-green hair behind her ear.
She looked down at Silas, her terrifying divine aura completely vanishing as she offered him a bright incredibly cute smile and waved happily at him.
"I did it, my Lord!" Eluned called out cheerfully.
"Did I do well?
Am I useful?"
Silas couldn’t help it.
He raised his Umbral-Forged Mythril Blade high into the air with the black metal catching the light of the morning sun finally breaking through the purple clouds.
"You did perfectly!" Silas shouted back to her, before turning to his awe-struck troops.
"Vanguard!
The dawn wave is broken!
The territory is secure!"
The twenty women stared at the decimated boss, stared at the Goddess, and then stared at their Lord.
And then, they erupted.
"FOR LORD GRAVES!" they screamed, a massive, deafening cheer of pure victory that echoed across the entire Umbral Basin.
They clashed their steel shields together and hoisted their bows into the air with their loyalty maxed out beyond measure.
As the cheers washed over him, a massive pristine golden tab suddenly materialized in front of Silas’s face.
It wasn’t a standard notification.
It was a global broadcast from the Sovereign Realm.
[Sovereign Realm Battle Assessment Complete...]
[Calculating Wave Survival...
Exceptional.]
[Calculating Threat Level Defeated: Over 100 Tier 2 Monsters + 1 Tier 3 Boss.]
[Location Modifier: Unknown Zone (Extreme Difficulty) applied.]
[Congratulations, Lord Silas Graves.]
[You have surpassed all standard metrics.
You have now become the #1 Territory on the Sovereign Newbie Leaderboards!]

chapters.title: Chapter 14: Blessed Land
paragraphs: The battlefield was completely silent, save for the crackle of dying pitch-fires in the trenches and the adrenaline-fueled breathing of the Vanguard.
Silas stood frozen in the center of the blood-soaked courtyard with his Umbral-Forged Mythril Blade hanging loosely from his grip.
He wasn’t looking at the two-mile-long trench Eluned had just carved through the necrotic forest...
He wasn’t looking at the mountain of steaming, mangled Tier 2 monster corpses piled high outside his Ironwood Palisade...
His blue eyes were locked squarely on the massive pristine golden tab hovering directly in the center of his vision.
[Sovereign Realm Battle Assessment Complete...]
[Calculating Wave Survival... Exceptional.]
[Calculating Threat Level Defeated: Over 100 Tier 2 Monsters + 1 Tier 3 Boss.]
[Location Modifier: Unknown Zone (Extreme Difficulty) applied.]
[Congratulations, Lord Silas Graves.]
[You have surpassed all standard metrics. You have now become the #1 Territory on the Sovereign Newbie Leaderboards!]
A cold shiver ran entirely down Silas’s spine.
For a brief second, the terrifying bruised-purple sky of the Umbral Basin faded away.
Silas’s mind violently snapped back to reality... back to the pristine, high-vaulted lecture halls of Valoria Academy.

He remembered sitting at his polished desk near the back of the class, an outcast scholarship student surrounded by the other people and heirs of megacorporations, listening to an elite instructor drone on about the survival rates in the Sovereign Realm.
’The Lord Alliance Board...’ Silas thought. ’It isn’t just a local ranking system, It’s the absolute metric of power for the entire human domain.’
He remembered the instructor pulling up a massive holographic projection of the leaderboards for the class.

They were strictly divided into two categories: [Classic], which held the monstrous centuries-old empires built by the ancient Lords, and [Newbie], which tracked the progress of the newly awakened Lords during their crucial first thirty days.
The scoring system was brutally simple.
One point for every standard monster killed within your territory’s borders.
Boss monsters offered massive point injections, and surviving in high-risk environments like an Unknown Zone provided astronomical multipliers.
Silas sighed with his grip tightening on the heavy leather hilt of his black sword.
’If you break into the Top 1,000 of the Classic section... The megacorporations offer you luxury contracts and if you break into the Top 100, the planetary government treats you like royalty.’
Silas mentally swiped his hand through the air, forcing his interface to open the full leaderboard.
A glowing blue list materialized in front of him.
[Sovereign Newbie Leaderboards - Day 2]
[Rank 1]: Unnamed Territory - 850 Points
[Rank 2]: House Sterling Garrison - 140 Points
[Rank 3]: Iron-Peak Citadel - 115 Points
[Rank 4]: Aegis of the Sun - 90 Points
[Rank 5]: Silver-Leaf Domain - 85 Points
Silas stared at the numbers in disbelief.
He wasn’t just in first place... He had absolutely shattered the curve.
The second-place holder, ’House Sterling’ which was undoubtedly one of those rich, arrogant noble heirs from one of the academies all over the world had 190... however Silas had 850.
’The Unknown Zone multiplier combined with a Tier 3 Boss kill...’ Silas thought. ’Sigh... what a good haul.’
But as his eyes scanned the glowing text, a slight frown touched his lips.
Every single territory below him had a grandiose imposing name.
His territory, the undisputed number one domain in the entire Newbie bracket, was listed simply as [Unnamed Territory].
"My Lord!"
Brida’s heavy armored boots crunched against the blood-stained dirt as she jogged up to him, instantly pulling him out of his internal interface.
The Shieldmaiden captain’s face was smeared with black soot and corrosive monster blood, but her eyes were shining with fanatical devotion.
Behind her, the remaining nineteen women of the Vanguard were lowering their weapons with the adrenaline finally bleeding out of their systems.
Tamsin was wiping her daggers on a clean patch of grass, while Rowena, the new B-Rank Rune Weaver, was leaning heavily against her staff, panting softly as her blue mana finally deactivated.
Eluned drifted down from the high palisade wall, landing gracefully beside Silas.
She didn’t have a single speck of dirt or ash on her flawless silver-green dress so she simply clung to his left arm, looking incredibly pleased with herself.
"We held the line, Lord Graves!" Brida reported, slamming her fist against her newly upgraded Steel Aegis.
The heavy metal rang like a cathedral bell. "The surviving beasts have completely routed and the perimeter is secure."
"You did more than hold the line, Brida..." Silas said as he looked at the twenty exhausted, bloodied women. "You slaughtered an army that would have wiped out any other territory in this realm."
He swiped his hand, projecting the [Newbie Leaderboard] tab outward so the girls could see it floating in the air.
"Because of your strength, we aren’t just surviving anymore," Silas announced.
He pointed to the massive 850 sitting at the absolute top of the list. "We are the strongest new territory in the Sovereign Realm."
The Vanguard stared at the glowing blue numbers. For a moment, they couldn’t fully comprehend it.

They were mortal summons, pulled from the ether to fight and die for a Lord but seeing the undeniable proof of their supremacy staring back at them caused a massive wave of overwhelming pride to wash through the ranks.
"Number one..." Fenna whispered, her grip tightening on her glowing magical recurve bow.
"Of course we are," Vanya laughed with the adrenaline spiking again. "Did you see what Lady Eluned did to that boss? Did you see the weapons the Lord pulled out of thin air? We are invincible!"
"There is just one problem..." Silas interrupted with a small amused smile touching his lips as he pointed to the top line. "We don’t have a name."
The girls blinked, looking at the [Unnamed Territory] designation.

"An empire cannot be nameless..." Silas said smoothly, crossing his arms over his chest. "You all fought for this dirt... You bled for it... So I want to hear your thoughts. What do we call our home?"
The Vanguard immediately perked up, deeply honored that their Lord was actually consulting them on a matter of absolute importance.
Most Lords viewed their summons as expendable tools, entirely beneath the right to speak.
Silas was actively treating them like his founding generals.

"We should call it the Blood-Gate!" Hilda, one of the new Heavy Shieldmaidens, shouted fiercely, slamming her broadsword against her shield. "To remind the monsters of what happens when they cross our threshold!"
"Too barbaric..." Alys countered, shaking her head. "We are an empire, not a raider camp. What about the Umbral Citadel?"
"That just names it after the disgusting beasts we just killed," Tamsin snorted while rolling her eyes.
Eluned tightened her grip on Silas’s arm as her eyes began glowing.
She looked up at him, completely ignoring the other girls.
"We should name it the Sanctuary of Graves. Or the Divine Realm of Silas. For wherever you stand, my Lord, the earth itself is sacred."
Silas violently coughed with his cheeks immediately flushing a deep crimson.
"Absolutely not," he shot down instantly. "I am not naming the territory after myself. That is painting a massive target on our backs for every Lord in the Newbie bracket."
He looked out past the heavy Ironwood gates.
He looked at the terrifying, necrotic treeline of the Umbral Basin, the bruised-purple sky, and the endless horrors lurking in the Unknown Zone.
This world was a literal nightmare of corruption and death.
But inside these walls, bathed in the golden light of the System and the emerald glow of Eluned’s magic, it was warm... It was safe... It was a haven carved out of hell itself...
"Blessed Land," Silas said quietly.
The Vanguard stopped bickering, turning to look at him.

"The Umbral Basin is cursed," Silas explained, his blue eyes sweeping over his territory. "It is meant to be a death sentence bbut we took root here anyway. With Eluned’s magic and your steel, this is the only piece of ground in the entire Unknown Zone that isn’t infected by the dark."
He looked at his troops.
"We will call it the Blessed Land."
A collective, massive smile spread across the faces of the twenty women.
It wasn’t overly aggressive, and it wasn’t arrogant. It was a perfect defiant statement against the horrors of the world they were trapped in.
"Blessed Land," Brida nodded firmly. "It is perfect, my Lord."
Silas focused his mind on the glowing digital interface.
[Would you like to officially name your territory ’Blessed Land’?]
’Accept...’ Silas commanded mentally.

The reaction was instantaneous as a warm cascading wave of brilliant golden light erupted from the center of the Keep, washing over the stone tiles scaling the massive Ironwood Palisade, and radiating out into the dark woods.
It was the cosmic law of the Sovereign Realm officially recognizing his authority over the coordinates.
[Territory Name Locked: Blessed Land.]
[Territory Aura Established: Morale decay negated within borders.]
"Alright," Silas clapped his hands together, shifting seamlessly back into commander mode. "We have the ranking, and we have the name. Now, let’s check the loot."
He pulled up his internal balance with his eyes scanning the final tally of Upgrade Points acquired from the massacre.
[Current Balance: 156 UP]

’Exactly 156,’ Silas thought, highly satisfied with the math. ’Upgrading the Vanguard’s gear mid-fight cost me a lot of UP, but the volume of the wave and the massive 20 UP injection from the Tier 3 Mini-Boss more than made up for it.’
"My Lord," Tamsin spoke up with her voice slicing through his internal calculations.
The Wilderness Huntress stepped forward, pointing her dagger toward the smoldering pitch-flooded trenches outside the gates.
"We have a massive logistical problem," Tamsin stated grimly.
Silas followed her gaze.
The adrenaline of the victory had temporarily masked the horrifying reality of the battlefield.
There were easily over a hundred massive, mangled corpses of Tier 2 Umbral Wolves, corrupted bears, and stone-scaled reptiles piled in the dirt.
At the very edge of the clearing lay the massive, twenty-foot lower half of the Tier 3 Boss Eluned had vaporized.

"The meat and the bone plating are incredibly valuable," Tamsin explained with her professional survivalist instincts kicking in. "But it seems we are in a high-mana density zone... If we leave them out there in the sun, the flesh will begin to rapidly rot within hours. The miasma from the corrosive blood will seep into the earth and poison our immediate perimeter and worse, the smell of a hundred rotting corpses will attract things far worse than wolves from deep within this place."
"Can we drag them into the courtyard?" Alys asked nervously.
"No," Brida shook her head. "We can’t pile rotting monster corpses in the middle of our barracks as the girls will get violently sick from the fumes."
Silas frowned.
Tamsin was right... They had fought a literal war to secure these resources, but they had absolutely nowhere to put them.
’I need a massive climate-controlled storage facility,’ Silas realized. ’And I need it right now.’
Silas swiped his hand, materializing the heavy leather-bound [Beginner Lord’s Manual] from his inventory.
He let the heavy book fall open in his hands, rapidly flipping through the thick paper pages until he hit the basic infrastructure blueprints provided to all new Lords by the Valoria City government.
His eyes scanned the glowing blue text etched into the pages.
[Construct Blueprint: Tier 1 Storage House]
[Requirements: 150 Units of Wood.]
[Description: A basic wooden warehouse used to shelter raw materials and resources from the elements. Does not prevent organic decay.]
Silas flipped the page again, looking ahead to his next most pressing issue.

’The girls have been living off processed military hardtack and dried meat...’ Silas thought, glancing at the exhausted troops. ’That is fine for a day or two, but long term, they will suffer from severe nutritional deficits. If they lose their combat efficiency, the territory falls so we need fresh food, and Eluned can probably grow anything if she has a proper enclosure.’
He found the corresponding blueprint.
[Construct Blueprint: Tier 1 Garden House]
[Requirements: 150 Units of Wood.]
[Description: A basic wooden enclosure with tilled earth... Protects fragile crops from harsh wind and does not possess climate control.]
Silas snapped the heavy book shut.

’I need 300 units of wood immediately,’ Silas calculated. ’I have the UP to forcefully evolve the buildings once they are placed hopefully, but the System physically cannot construct the Tier 1 base models unless I provide the exact raw materials required by the cosmic laws.’

"Vanguard, listen to me!" Silas barked, pointing toward the massive pile of corpses outside the gates. "Brida, organize a hauling team! I want those corpses dragged out of the trenches and lined up neatly inside the courtyard immediately!"
"Yes, my Lord!" Brida saluted perfectly, turning to her troops. "Shieldmaidens, with me! Put your backs into it!"
"Tamsin, Rowena, Fenna," Silas ordered the lighter-armored girls. "Set up a perimeter at the edge of the treeline and keep your eyes peeled for scavengers."
As the girls immediately sprinted off to execute his orders, the physical exertion of dragging multi-ton monsters taking a massive toll on the Shieldmaidens, Silas turned to Eluned.
The Goddess was standing patiently by his side, her hands clasped in front of her.
"Eluned," Silas said. "I need your help."
"Anything you desire, my Lord..." Eluned replied instantly.
Silas walked her out past the heavy Ironwood gates, past the hauling teams dragging massive wolves through the dirt, and stopped right at the edge of the necrotic treeline.
Towering, fifty-foot Ironwood trees loomed over them, their bark as hard as tempered steel.
Silas opened the [Beginner Lord’s Manual] and pointed to a small diagram on the page.

"I need three hundred units of wood," Silas explained, tapping the diagram. "A ’unit’ in the Sovereign Realm isn’t just a log... It has to be perfectly cut into standardized, interlocking blocks, roughly two feet by two feet. Normally, a Lord would have to summon fifty lumberjacks and spend three days hacking away at these trees with iron axes to get enough refined material."
He looked up at the Goddess. "Can you do it?"
Eluned looked at the diagram in the book, then looked up at the massive, steel-hard Ironwood trees and then she let out a soft musical giggle that sounded like wind chimes.
"My Lord," Eluned smiled, looking at him with genuine amusement. "I am a Goddess of the World Tree. The forest does not resist me... It obeys me."
She took a single, graceful step forward, placing her delicate, pale hand gently against the thick black bark of the nearest fifty-foot Ironwood tree.
Eluned didn’t exert any visible physical effort as she simply let her SSS-Rank divine aura bleed into the earth.
"Rise," Eluned whispered.
The ground violently completely ruptured.
Silas stumbled back a step as massive glowing, semi-translucent green roots exploded from the black soil.
The divine roots wrapped around the base of the towering Ironwood tree like the tentacles of a colossal kraken.

With a sickening, deafening CRACK that echoed over a long distance, the roots effortlessly snapped the tree’s deep subterranean anchors and hoisted the entire fifty-foot multi-ton trunk directly into the air.
"Gods..." Tamsin gasped from her perimeter post with her jaw completely dropping as she watched the Goddess casually levitate a tree that weighed more than a siege engine.
Eluned didn’t stop there.
She raised her other hand, her emerald eyes glowing with terrifying precision as she swiped her index finger horizontally through the air in a rapid fluid motion.
SHING! SHING! SHING! SHING!
Dozens of hyper-compressed, razor-thin wind blades materialized out of thin air.
They shot forward at supersonic speeds, creating sharp vacuum cracks as they impacted the suspended Ironwood.
The steel-hard bark offered absolutely zero resistance.
Silas watched in flabbergasted awe as the wind blades perfectly, flawlessly diced the massive tree.
It looked like a master chef rapidly slicing a carrot.
The branches were sheared off and discarded into the forest, while the main trunk was violently cut into exact... perfectly symmetrical, two-foot-by-two-foot interlocking blocks of refined Ironwood.
The perfectly standardized units of wood rained down from the sky, thudding heavily against the dirt in incredibly neat, organized piles.
Eluned stepped to the next tree.
"Rise..." she commanded again.
Within exactly ninety seconds, Eluned had effortlessly uprooted and flawlessly processed seven massive Ironwood trees.
Three hundred perfectly cut units of refined wood sat in pristine stacks on the edge of the treeline.
Eluned lowered her hands with the glowing green roots retreating seamlessly back into the earth.
She turned around, brushing her silver-green hair behind her ear and looked at Silas with an incredibly bright, expectant smile.
"Is this sufficient for your needs, Lord Graves?" Eluned asked, rocking slightly on her heels.
Silas stared at the massive mountain of perfectly refined wood.
He stared at the Goddess who had just casually broken every law of physics and logistics in the Sovereign Realm without breaking a single drop of sweat.
Silas didn’t say a word.
He just walked up to her, raised his hand, and gently placed it on the top of her head.
He ruffled her silver-green hair, giving her a deeply affectionate headpat.
"You are absolutely unbelievable," Silas murmured with a smile breaking across his face. "Thank you."
Eluned completely melted.
A furious burning blush instantly consumed her pale face, spreading all the way to the tips of her slightly pointed ears.
She closed her eyes, leaning heavily into his touch letting out a soft incredibly happy sigh.
’If the other Lords could see me right now, they would vomit blood in sheer envy...’ Silas thought.
Silas swept his hand over the piles of wood with his Lord inventory automatically activating.
The heavy Ironwood blocks vanished into the ether, perfectly syncing with his internal storage.
[Inventory Updated: Ironwood - 300 / 300 Units]
He had the materials... He had the UP... It was time to build.

sentences.text: The battlefield was completely silent, save for the crackle of dying pitch-fires in the trenches and the adrenaline-fueled breathing of the Vanguard.
Silas stood frozen in the center of the blood-soaked courtyard with his Umbral-Forged Mythril Blade hanging loosely from his grip.
He wasn’t looking at the two-mile-long trench Eluned had just carved through the necrotic forest...
He wasn’t looking at the mountain of steaming, mangled Tier 2 monster corpses piled high outside his Ironwood Palisade...
His blue eyes were locked squarely on the massive pristine golden tab hovering directly in the center of his vision.
[Sovereign Realm Battle Assessment Complete...]
[Calculating Wave Survival...
Exceptional.]
[Calculating Threat Level Defeated: Over 100 Tier 2 Monsters + 1 Tier 3 Boss.]
[Location Modifier: Unknown Zone (Extreme Difficulty) applied.]
[Congratulations, Lord Silas Graves.]
[You have surpassed all standard metrics.
You have now become the #1 Territory on the Sovereign Newbie Leaderboards!]
A cold shiver ran entirely down Silas’s spine.
For a brief second, the terrifying bruised-purple sky of the Umbral Basin faded away.
Silas’s mind violently snapped back to reality... back to the pristine, high-vaulted lecture halls of Valoria Academy.

He remembered sitting at his polished desk near the back of the class, an outcast scholarship student surrounded by the other people and heirs of megacorporations, listening to an elite instructor drone on about the survival rates in the Sovereign Realm.
’The Lord Alliance Board...’ Silas thought. ’It isn’t just a local ranking system, It’s the absolute metric of power for the entire human domain.’
He remembered the instructor pulling up a massive holographic projection of the leaderboards for the class.

They were strictly divided into two categories: [Classic], which held the monstrous centuries-old empires built by the ancient Lords, and [Newbie], which tracked the progress of the newly awakened Lords during their crucial first thirty days.
The scoring system was brutally simple.
One point for every standard monster killed within your territory’s borders.
Boss monsters offered massive point injections, and surviving in high-risk environments like an Unknown Zone provided astronomical multipliers.
Silas sighed with his grip tightening on the heavy leather hilt of his black sword.
’If you break into the Top 1,000 of the Classic section...
The megacorporations offer you luxury contracts and if you break into the Top 100, the planetary government treats you like royalty.’
Silas mentally swiped his hand through the air, forcing his interface to open the full leaderboard.
A glowing blue list materialized in front of him.
[Sovereign Newbie Leaderboards - Day 2]
[Rank 1]: Unnamed Territory - 850 Points
[Rank 2]: House Sterling Garrison - 140 Points
[Rank 3]: Iron-Peak Citadel - 115 Points
[Rank 4]: Aegis of the Sun - 90 Points
[Rank 5]: Silver-Leaf Domain - 85 Points
Silas stared at the numbers in disbelief.
He wasn’t just in first place...
He had absolutely shattered the curve.
The second-place holder, ’House Sterling’ which was undoubtedly one of those rich, arrogant noble heirs from one of the academies all over the world had 190... however Silas had 850.
’The Unknown Zone multiplier combined with a Tier 3 Boss kill...’ Silas thought. ’Sigh... what a good haul.’
But as his eyes scanned the glowing text, a slight frown touched his lips.
Every single territory below him had a grandiose imposing name.
His territory, the undisputed number one domain in the entire Newbie bracket, was listed simply as [Unnamed Territory].
"My Lord!"
Brida’s heavy armored boots crunched against the blood-stained dirt as she jogged up to him, instantly pulling him out of his internal interface.
The Shieldmaiden captain’s face was smeared with black soot and corrosive monster blood, but her eyes were shining with fanatical devotion.
Behind her, the remaining nineteen women of the Vanguard were lowering their weapons with the adrenaline finally bleeding out of their systems.
Tamsin was wiping her daggers on a clean patch of grass, while Rowena, the new B-Rank Rune Weaver, was leaning heavily against her staff, panting softly as her blue mana finally deactivated.
Eluned drifted down from the high palisade wall, landing gracefully beside Silas.
She didn’t have a single speck of dirt or ash on her flawless silver-green dress so she simply clung to his left arm, looking incredibly pleased with herself.
"We held the line, Lord Graves!" Brida reported, slamming her fist against her newly upgraded Steel Aegis.
The heavy metal rang like a cathedral bell.
"The surviving beasts have completely routed and the perimeter is secure."
"You did more than hold the line, Brida..." Silas said as he looked at the twenty exhausted, bloodied women.
"You slaughtered an army that would have wiped out any other territory in this realm."
He swiped his hand, projecting the [Newbie Leaderboard] tab outward so the girls could see it floating in the air.
"Because of your strength, we aren’t just surviving anymore," Silas announced.
He pointed to the massive 850 sitting at the absolute top of the list.
"We are the strongest new territory in the Sovereign Realm."
The Vanguard stared at the glowing blue numbers.
For a moment, they couldn’t fully comprehend it.

They were mortal summons, pulled from the ether to fight and die for a Lord but seeing the undeniable proof of their supremacy staring back at them caused a massive wave of overwhelming pride to wash through the ranks.
"Number one..." Fenna whispered, her grip tightening on her glowing magical recurve bow.
"Of course we are," Vanya laughed with the adrenaline spiking again.
"Did you see what Lady Eluned did to that boss?
Did you see the weapons the Lord pulled out of thin air?
We are invincible!"
"There is just one problem..." Silas interrupted with a small amused smile touching his lips as he pointed to the top line.
"We don’t have a name."
The girls blinked, looking at the [Unnamed Territory] designation.
"An empire cannot be nameless..." Silas said smoothly, crossing his arms over his chest.
"You all fought for this dirt...
You bled for it...
So I want to hear your thoughts.
What do we call our home?"
The Vanguard immediately perked up, deeply honored that their Lord was actually consulting them on a matter of absolute importance.
Most Lords viewed their summons as expendable tools, entirely beneath the right to speak.
Silas was actively treating them like his founding generals.
"We should call it the Blood-Gate!" Hilda, one of the new Heavy Shieldmaidens, shouted fiercely, slamming her broadsword against her shield.
"To remind the monsters of what happens when they cross our threshold!"
"Too barbaric..." Alys countered, shaking her head.
"We are an empire, not a raider camp.
What about the Umbral Citadel?"
"That just names it after the disgusting beasts we just killed," Tamsin snorted while rolling her eyes.
Eluned tightened her grip on Silas’s arm as her eyes began glowing.
She looked up at him, completely ignoring the other girls.
"We should name it the Sanctuary of Graves.
Or the Divine Realm of Silas.
For wherever you stand, my Lord, the earth itself is sacred."
Silas violently coughed with his cheeks immediately flushing a deep crimson.
"Absolutely not," he shot down instantly.
"I am not naming the territory after myself.
That is painting a massive target on our backs for every Lord in the Newbie bracket."
He looked out past the heavy Ironwood gates.
He looked at the terrifying, necrotic treeline of the Umbral Basin, the bruised-purple sky, and the endless horrors lurking in the Unknown Zone.
This world was a literal nightmare of corruption and death.
But inside these walls, bathed in the golden light of the System and the emerald glow of Eluned’s magic, it was warm...
It was safe...
It was a haven carved out of hell itself...
"Blessed Land," Silas said quietly.
The Vanguard stopped bickering, turning to look at him.
"The Umbral Basin is cursed," Silas explained, his blue eyes sweeping over his territory.
"It is meant to be a death sentence bbut we took root here anyway.
With Eluned’s magic and your steel, this is the only piece of ground in the entire Unknown Zone that isn’t infected by the dark."
He looked at his troops.
"We will call it the Blessed Land."
A collective, massive smile spread across the faces of the twenty women.
It wasn’t overly aggressive, and it wasn’t arrogant.
It was a perfect defiant statement against the horrors of the world they were trapped in.
"Blessed Land," Brida nodded firmly.
"It is perfect, my Lord."
Silas focused his mind on the glowing digital interface.
[Would you like to officially name your territory ’Blessed Land’?]
’Accept...’ Silas commanded mentally.

The reaction was instantaneous as a warm cascading wave of brilliant golden light erupted from the center of the Keep, washing over the stone tiles scaling the massive Ironwood Palisade, and radiating out into the dark woods.
It was the cosmic law of the Sovereign Realm officially recognizing his authority over the coordinates.
[Territory Name Locked: Blessed Land.]
[Territory Aura Established: Morale decay negated within borders.]
"Alright," Silas clapped his hands together, shifting seamlessly back into commander mode.
"We have the ranking, and we have the name.
Now, let’s check the loot."
He pulled up his internal balance with his eyes scanning the final tally of Upgrade Points acquired from the massacre.
[Current Balance: 156 UP]

’Exactly 156,’ Silas thought, highly satisfied with the math. ’Upgrading the Vanguard’s gear mid-fight cost me a lot of UP, but the volume of the wave and the massive 20 UP injection from the Tier 3 Mini-Boss more than made up for it.’
"My Lord," Tamsin spoke up with her voice slicing through his internal calculations.
The Wilderness Huntress stepped forward, pointing her dagger toward the smoldering pitch-flooded trenches outside the gates.
"We have a massive logistical problem," Tamsin stated grimly.
Silas followed her gaze.
The adrenaline of the victory had temporarily masked the horrifying reality of the battlefield.
There were easily over a hundred massive, mangled corpses of Tier 2 Umbral Wolves, corrupted bears, and stone-scaled reptiles piled in the dirt.
At the very edge of the clearing lay the massive, twenty-foot lower half of the Tier 3 Boss Eluned had vaporized.
"The meat and the bone plating are incredibly valuable," Tamsin explained with her professional survivalist instincts kicking in.
"But it seems we are in a high-mana density zone...
If we leave them out there in the sun, the flesh will begin to rapidly rot within hours.

The miasma from the corrosive blood will seep into the earth and poison our immediate perimeter and worse, the smell of a hundred rotting corpses will attract things far worse than wolves from deep within this place."
"Can we drag them into the courtyard?" Alys asked nervously.
"No," Brida shook her head.
"We can’t pile rotting monster corpses in the middle of our barracks as the girls will get violently sick from the fumes."
Silas frowned.
Tamsin was right...
They had fought a literal war to secure these resources, but they had absolutely nowhere to put them.
’I need a massive climate-controlled storage facility,’ Silas realized. ’And I need it right now.’
Silas swiped his hand, materializing the heavy leather-bound [Beginner Lord’s Manual] from his inventory.
He let the heavy book fall open in his hands, rapidly flipping through the thick paper pages until he hit the basic infrastructure blueprints provided to all new Lords by the Valoria City government.
His eyes scanned the glowing blue text etched into the pages.
[Construct Blueprint: Tier 1 Storage House]
[Requirements: 150 Units of Wood.]
[Description: A basic wooden warehouse used to shelter raw materials and resources from the elements.
Does not prevent organic decay.]
Silas flipped the page again, looking ahead to his next most pressing issue.

’The girls have been living off processed military hardtack and dried meat...’ Silas thought, glancing at the exhausted troops. ’That is fine for a day or two, but long term, they will suffer from severe nutritional deficits.
If they lose their combat efficiency, the territory falls so we need fresh food, and Eluned can probably grow anything if she has a proper enclosure.’
He found the corresponding blueprint.
[Construct Blueprint: Tier 1 Garden House]
[Requirements: 150 Units of Wood.]

Protects fragile crops from harsh wind and does not possess climate control.]

’I need 300 units of wood immediately,’ Silas calculated. ’I have the UP to forcefully evolve the buildings once they are placed hopefully, but the System physically cannot construct the Tier 1 base models unless I provide the exact raw materials required by the cosmic laws.’
"Vanguard, listen to me!" Silas barked, pointing toward the massive pile of corpses outside the gates.

I want those corpses dragged out of the trenches and lined up neatly inside the courtyard immediately!"

chapters.title: Chapter 15: Build... Build... And Build!
paragraphs: The cold biting wind of the Umbral Basin whipped across the courtyard as Silas and Eluned walked back through the heavy Ironwood gates of the Blessed Land.
Inside the palisade walls, the Vanguard had executed his orders flawlessly.

The massive mangled corpses of over a hundred Tier 2 Spirit Beasts along with the colossal twenty-foot lower half of the Corrupted Ursine Overlord were laid out in neat, highly organized rows across the southern half of the stone tiles.
The sheer volume of resources was staggering and the amount of blood soaking into the ground was equally alarming.
"The perimeter is entirely secure, my Lord!" Brida called out, stepping away from the line of corpses.
Her Steel Aegis was strapped firmly to her back. "The hauling is complete but the miasma is already growing thick. If we don’t process these beasts soon, the fumes will become toxic."
"I am handling it right now..." Silas assured her with his blue eyes sweeping over the mountain of loot.
He walked directly into the center of the northern, empty half of his courtyard.
The stone tiles here were clean, unblemished by the battle and it was the perfect foundation for his infrastructure expansion.
Silas pulled up his internal interface with his eyes briefly glancing at the glowing golden numbers in the corner of his vision.
[Current Balance: 156 UP]

’One hundred and fifty-six,’ Silas thought as he saw it again. ’I have exactly enough to solve our logistics and our food supply in one sweeping motion but I can’t afford to make a single mistake. I need to squeeze every ounce of value out of these points.’
Putting those thoughts aside, Silas focused.
Hovering right in the center of his vision, a brilliant blue holographic projection materialized.

His Lord inventory had automatically synced with the Build Function, instantly reading the materials he had just acquired from the edge of the forest as a distinct resource tab appeared in the center of the projection.
[Ironwood: 300 / 300 Units]
Silas mentally partitioned exactly half of the refined timber for his first project.

He targeted a large open fifty-by-fifty foot square of stone tiles on the eastern edge of the courtyard and he focused his mind on the structure, and the interface provided a crisp updated description.
[Tier 1 Storage House]

[Description]: Contains 150 units of Ironwood... Sufficient to construct a Tier 1 Storage House. A basic wooden warehouse used to shelter raw materials and resources from the elements and does not prevent organic decay.
Silas didn’t hesitate for a fraction of a second.
’Construct...’ he commanded mentally.

Instantly, the resource tab shattered into a violent storm of pixelated light as a massive rushing wind billowed outward from the center of the courtyard, kicking up the dust and violently snapping the heavy cloaks of the Vanguard.
The holographic blue wireframe suddenly began to fill with physical matter.
Heavy blocks of perfectly refined Ironwood slammed down from the ether, stacking perfectly upon one another with deafening thuds.
Thick beams slotted into place, forming a massive interlocking wooden foundation.
The walls shot upward, and a heavy sloped timber roof slammed down from the sky to cap the structure perfectly.
The entire process took less than ten seconds.
A blinding flash of white light signaled the final culmination of the architecture, leaving a massive highly durable wooden warehouse sitting squarely on the stone tiles of the Blessed Land.
"Whoa!" Fenna gasped, shielding her eyes from the sudden flash of light.
Silas walked up to the heavy wooden double doors and tapped his palm against the rough bark.
[Storage House]
[Tier]: 1 Construct (Common)
[Durability]: 300 / 300

’It’s huge, but it’s fundamentally just a wooden box...’ Silas analyzed instantly. ’There is absolutely zero climate control. If we put the meat in there right now, it will just rot in the shade instead of the sun so the miasma would still build up inside until the building becomes a literal gas chamber.’
The reason he was so confident about being able to eat Monster meat was that meat in the Sovereign Realm unless they were really acidic and even then, A Lord could still eat it without dying.
It was time to force an evolution.
Silas focused his mind squarely on the glowing golden tab hovering directly above the structure’s durability readout.
[Would you like to upgrade Tier 1 Storage House to Tier 2 Frost-Sealed Vault?]
[Cost: 70 UP]
’Accept...’ Silas commanded without a second thought.
The courtyard was instantly plunged into a blinding radiance.
A towering pillar of incandescent golden light erupted directly from Silas’s palm, completely engulfing the massive wooden warehouse.

The sheer magical pressure of the Absolute Upgrade System descending upon the physical realm caused the air temperature in the courtyard to instantly plummet, sending a wave of biting freezing cold rushing outward.
Inside the golden pillar, the structure was being fundamentally rewritten by the cosmic laws.
The simple wooden walls darkened, becoming hyper-dense and thoroughly insulated.
The basic iron hinges melted and rapidly reformed into heavy dense mythril locking mechanisms capable of sealing an airtight vault.
When the light finally shattered like glass and faded into the ether, a completely new breathtakingly advanced facility rested in the courtyard.
It was a veritable fortress of preservation as deep, chilling blue mist actively rolled out from the bottom of the heavy reinforced steel doors.
Silas gripped the mythril handle and heaved the massive doors open.
’Damn... I really love upgrading stuff.’
The Vanguard gasped collectively.
The interior wasn’t just an empty, dark room anymore... The system had provided a full suite of Tier 2 utility.
The massive insulated walls were lined with intricate, glowing blue frost-runes keeping the ambient temperature at a perfect, meat-preserving deep freeze.
Down the center of the massive room sat pristine heavy steel butchery tables, large enchanted wooden bowls for blood-letting and racks of heavy, razor-sharp iron meat cleavers.
"By the gods..." Tamsin whispered with her professional eyes wide as she stepped past Silas into the freezing mist of the vault.
She ran a hand over the pristine steel of a butchery table. "This is... this is perfect. It’s an absolute masterpiece. We can store the entire horde in here and the meat won’t decay for a long time."

"Then let’s not waste any time," Silas smiled, thoroughly satisfied with the investment. "Tamsin, you are officially in charge of the harvest... Take whoever you need... Strip the bone plating, save the pelts, drain the corrosive blood into the enchanted bowls, and secure the meat."
"With extreme pleasure, my Lord!" Tamsin saluted enthusiastically with a wicked grin spreading across her face.
She immediately turned to the Vanguard. "Brida! Get the Shieldmaidens! Start hauling the wolves in here! Fenna, grab a cleaver! We have a mountain to carve!"
The Vanguard operated like a well-oiled machine.
Within seconds, the girls were dragging the massive corpses into the freezing mist of the vault with the heavy thwack of meat cleavers and the sound of peeling leather quickly filling the air.
Silas didn’t stop to rest.
He turned his attention back to the courtyard.
He walked to the final empty quadrant of the Blessed Land, placing himself a respectful distance away from both the Armored Barracks and the new Frost-Sealed Vault.
Silas pulled up the interface again with his inventory automatically syncing his remaining lumber.
[Ironwood: 150 / 150]
[Construct Blueprint: Tier 1 Garden House]

[Description]: Contains 150 units of Ironwood... Sufficient to construct a Tier 1 Garden House. A basic wooden enclosure with tilled earth that protects fragile crops from harsh wind and does not possess climate control.
Silas focused his intent.
’Construct.’
Once again, the resource tab shattered into pixelated light. The rushing wind kicked up, howling through the courtyard as the blue holographic wireframe anchored itself to the stone.
Heavy beams of perfectly refined Ironwood slammed down from the sky, interlocking with brutal efficiency.
Within ten seconds, a long, low-slung wooden enclosure with a slanted roof materialized.
Silas stepped up to the basic wooden structure and placed his hand against the door.
[Would you like to upgrade Tier 1 Garden House to Tier 2 Verdant Conservatory?]
[Cost: 76 UP]
Silas mentally verified his math one last time.
He had 86 UP remaining. This upgrade would cost 76, leaving him with exactly 10 UP—a razor-thin margin but an absolutely necessary expenditure.
’I’m glad these ones are cheap... Accept!’ Silas commanded.
The final surge of golden light erupted from his hands, violently restructuring the basic wood.
His internal interface chimed as his UP balance aggressively ticked down.
[Current Balance: 10 UP]
When the blinding light faded, the basic wooden shack was completely gone. In its place stood a breathtakingly beautiful, magically climate-controlled glass-and-wood conservatory.
The enchanted glass panels spanning the roof and walls hummed with a warm golden light, specifically designed by the System to trap and amplify the ambient mana of the Sovereign Realm.
’Amazing...’ Eluned thought from beside him.
Silas pushed the elegant heavy timber door open and stepped inside.
The air within the Conservatory was a stark contrast to the freezing, biting wind of the Umbral Basin.
It was incredibly warm and rich, smelling heavily of fresh rain and deeply fertile soil.
Long, perfectly pristine beds of black nutrient-dense earth stretched out before him, separated by neat stone walkways.

It was the perfect environment to grow anything but as Silas looked at the perfectly tilled empty dirt as the massive adrenaline high of building the territory suddenly crashed into a suffocating wall of realization.
Silas stopped walking, his shoulders slumping slightly.
’I’m an idiot,’ Silas thought, mentally kicking himself as he stared at the barren soil. ’I am a colossal idiot.’
He had a Tier 2 magical greenhouse. The soil was so rich it practically hummed with potential but he had absolutely nothing to plant in it.
Silas had forgotten to buy seeds!

’Without seeds, this Conservatory is just a highly expensive glowing empty room...’ Silas lamented, running a hand through his dark hair. ’The girls can’t eat dirt, no matter how magically rich it is... They need actual nutrition to maintain their combat efficiency and high-tier crops sell for a fortune on the market.’
"Do not worry, my Lord..." a soft melodic voice whispered right beside his ear.
Silas turned his head, slightly startled.
Eluned had followed him silently inside. The Goddess of the World Tree stepped delicately past him, walking out into the center of the massive, empty dirt beds.
She looked back at him as her emerald eyes glowed with a comforting warmth.
"You forget who I am," Eluned smiled gently.
She didn’t wait for his response.
The Goddess knelt gracefully onto the black earth, completely unconcerned about the damp soil staining the hem of her flawless silver-green dress.
She pressed her delicate, pale hands completely flat against the empty, seedless dirt and she closed her eyes and let out a deep, slow breath.
Silas watched as her divine SSS-Rank aura flared to life.
It wasn’t the violent hyper-pressurized wind magic that she had used to obliterate the Ironwood trees.
This was completely different...
[Aura of Genesis: Spontaneous Cultivation]
It was an undisputed miracle.
From the completely barren dirt beneath her hands, tiny sparks of glowing emerald light began to aggressively bubble to the surface.
Within a fraction of a second, vibrant glowing green shoots violently erupted from the soil.
The SSS-Rank divine magic completely bypassed the biological necessity of seeds.𝗳𝐫𝚎𝗲𝚠𝚎𝗯𝕟𝐨𝘃𝚎𝗹.𝗰𝗼𝗺
Eluned didn’t just manipulate nature... she was nature and she was actively commanding the ambient mana trapped within the Conservatory to take physical organic form.
Before Silas’s very eyes, the entire length of the eighty-foot Conservatory exploded into life.
The growth was exponential and instantaneous.
Massive, glowing red fruits the size of melons rapidly expanded and hung heavily from thick sturdy vines that climbed the enchanted glass walls.

Dense, highly nutritious leafy greens sprouted in perfectly organized rows along the soil beds and shimmering golden wheat that radiated pure mana shot up to waist height in a matter of seconds, fully maturing instantly.
The scent of blooming flowers, sweet fruit, and fresh rain completely filled the enclosure.
The empty room had been transformed into a breathtaking literal Garden of Eden overflowing with high-tier magical crops.
Eluned stood up, wiping a speck of rich black dirt from her knee. She looked proudly at the massive harvest with her chest heaving slightly from the exertion, before turning back to her Lord.

"The Blessed Land will never go hungry..." Eluned stated softly with a deeply satisfied smile gracing her lips. "These are Spirit-Fruits and Ether-Wheat. They will restore stamina, enhance mana recovery, and nourish the Vanguard far better than salted meat."
Silas stared at the glowing fruits and then his chest swelled with an overwhelming sense of victory that completely dwarfed his earlier realization of the Leaderboard ranking.
The territory was completely secure.

The Vanguard was heavily armed with Steel and magical bows... They had a mountain of Tier 2 monster meat and bone plating safely preserved in a freezing vault and now, they had a literal paradise of magical crops growing indefinitely within their walls.
They were fully, entirely self-sustaining in the middle of a literal death zone.
Silas stepped forward, crossing the stone walkway, and wrapped his arms firmly around Eluned, pulling her into a tight warm embrace.
He rested his chin gently on the top of her silver-green head.
"Thank you Eluned," Silas whispered into the quiet glowing greenhouse. "Truly."
Eluned gasped softly, her breath hitching in her throat.
Her arms quickly wrapped tightly around his waist as she buried her furiously blushing face deep into his chest.
She could hear his heart beating steadily against her ear.
Surrounded by the miraculous life she had just created, the SSS-Rank Goddess completely surrendered to the overwhelming protectiveness and genuine gratitude radiating from her Lord.
She held him tightly, absolutely certain that the Blessed Land was exactly where she belonged.

sentences.text: The cold biting wind of the Umbral Basin whipped across the courtyard as Silas and Eluned walked back through the heavy Ironwood gates of the Blessed Land.
Inside the palisade walls, the Vanguard had executed his orders flawlessly.

The massive mangled corpses of over a hundred Tier 2 Spirit Beasts along with the colossal twenty-foot lower half of the Corrupted Ursine Overlord were laid out in neat, highly organized rows across the southern half of the stone tiles.
The sheer volume of resources was staggering and the amount of blood soaking into the ground was equally alarming.
"The perimeter is entirely secure, my Lord!" Brida called out, stepping away from the line of corpses.
Her Steel Aegis was strapped firmly to her back.
"The hauling is complete but the miasma is already growing thick.
If we don’t process these beasts soon, the fumes will become toxic."
"I am handling it right now..." Silas assured her with his blue eyes sweeping over the mountain of loot.

[Current Balance: 156 UP]

Sufficient to construct a Tier 1 Storage House.
A basic wooden warehouse used to shelter raw materials and resources from the elements and does not prevent organic decay.

’Construct...’ he commanded mentally.

Instantly, the resource tab shattered into a violent storm of pixelated light as a massive rushing wind billowed outward from the center of the courtyard, kicking up the dust and violently snapping the heavy cloaks of the Vanguard.
The holographic blue wireframe suddenly began to fill with physical matter.
Heavy blocks of perfectly refined Ironwood slammed down from the ether, stacking perfectly upon one another with deafening thuds.
Thick beams slotted into place, forming a massive interlocking wooden foundation.
The walls shot upward, and a heavy sloped timber roof slammed down from the sky to cap the structure perfectly.
The entire process took less than ten seconds.
A blinding flash of white light signaled the final culmination of the architecture, leaving a massive highly durable wooden warehouse sitting squarely on the stone tiles of the Blessed Land.
"Whoa!" Fenna gasped, shielding her eyes from the sudden flash of light.
Silas walked up to the heavy wooden double doors and tapped his palm against the rough bark.
[Storage House]
[Tier]: 1 Construct (Common)
[Durability]: 300 / 300
’It’s huge, but it’s fundamentally just a wooden box...’ Silas analyzed instantly. ’There is absolutely zero climate control.
If we put the meat in there right now, it will just rot in the shade instead of the sun so the miasma would still build up inside until the building becomes a literal gas chamber.’
The reason he was so confident about being able to eat Monster meat was that meat in the Sovereign Realm unless they were really acidic and even then, A Lord could still eat it without dying.
It was time to force an evolution.
Silas focused his mind squarely on the glowing golden tab hovering directly above the structure’s durability readout.
[Would you like to upgrade Tier 1 Storage House to Tier 2 Frost-Sealed Vault?]
[Cost: 70 UP]
’Accept...’ Silas commanded without a second thought.
The courtyard was instantly plunged into a blinding radiance.
A towering pillar of incandescent golden light erupted directly from Silas’s palm, completely engulfing the massive wooden warehouse.

The sheer magical pressure of the Absolute Upgrade System descending upon the physical realm caused the air temperature in the courtyard to instantly plummet, sending a wave of biting freezing cold rushing outward.
Inside the golden pillar, the structure was being fundamentally rewritten by the cosmic laws.
The simple wooden walls darkened, becoming hyper-dense and thoroughly insulated.
The basic iron hinges melted and rapidly reformed into heavy dense mythril locking mechanisms capable of sealing an airtight vault.
When the light finally shattered like glass and faded into the ether, a completely new breathtakingly advanced facility rested in the courtyard.
It was a veritable fortress of preservation as deep, chilling blue mist actively rolled out from the bottom of the heavy reinforced steel doors.
Silas gripped the mythril handle and heaved the massive doors open.
’Damn...
I really love upgrading stuff.’
The Vanguard gasped collectively.
The interior wasn’t just an empty, dark room anymore...
The system had provided a full suite of Tier 2 utility.
The massive insulated walls were lined with intricate, glowing blue frost-runes keeping the ambient temperature at a perfect, meat-preserving deep freeze.
Down the center of the massive room sat pristine heavy steel butchery tables, large enchanted wooden bowls for blood-letting and racks of heavy, razor-sharp iron meat cleavers.
"By the gods..." Tamsin whispered with her professional eyes wide as she stepped past Silas into the freezing mist of the vault.
She ran a hand over the pristine steel of a butchery table.
"This is... this is perfect.
It’s an absolute masterpiece.
We can store the entire horde in here and the meat won’t decay for a long time."
"Then let’s not waste any time," Silas smiled, thoroughly satisfied with the investment.
"Tamsin, you are officially in charge of the harvest...
Take whoever you need...
Strip the bone plating, save the pelts, drain the corrosive blood into the enchanted bowls, and secure the meat."
"With extreme pleasure, my Lord!" Tamsin saluted enthusiastically with a wicked grin spreading across her face.
She immediately turned to the Vanguard.
"Brida!
Get the Shieldmaidens!
Start hauling the wolves in here!
Fenna, grab a cleaver!
We have a mountain to carve!"
The Vanguard operated like a well-oiled machine.
Within seconds, the girls were dragging the massive corpses into the freezing mist of the vault with the heavy thwack of meat cleavers and the sound of peeling leather quickly filling the air.
Silas didn’t stop to rest.
He turned his attention back to the courtyard.
He walked to the final empty quadrant of the Blessed Land, placing himself a respectful distance away from both the Armored Barracks and the new Frost-Sealed Vault.
Silas pulled up the interface again with his inventory automatically syncing his remaining lumber.
[Ironwood: 150 / 150]
[Construct Blueprint: Tier 1 Garden House]
[Description]: Contains 150 units of Ironwood...
Sufficient to construct a Tier 1 Garden House.
A basic wooden enclosure with tilled earth that protects fragile crops from harsh wind and does not possess climate control.
Silas focused his intent.
’Construct.’
Once again, the resource tab shattered into pixelated light.
The rushing wind kicked up, howling through the courtyard as the blue holographic wireframe anchored itself to the stone.
Heavy beams of perfectly refined Ironwood slammed down from the sky, interlocking with brutal efficiency.
Within ten seconds, a long, low-slung wooden enclosure with a slanted roof materialized.
Silas stepped up to the basic wooden structure and placed his hand against the door.
[Would you like to upgrade Tier 1 Garden House to Tier 2 Verdant Conservatory?]
[Cost: 76 UP]

He had 86 UP remaining.
This upgrade would cost 76, leaving him with exactly 10 UP—a razor-thin margin but an absolutely necessary expenditure.
’I’m glad these ones are cheap...
Accept!’ Silas commanded.
The final surge of golden light erupted from his hands, violently restructuring the basic wood.
His internal interface chimed as his UP balance aggressively ticked down.

In its place stood a breathtakingly beautiful, magically climate-controlled glass-and-wood conservatory.
