chapters.title: Chapter 33: Going To War [II]
paragraphs: The newbies violently snapped out of their paralyzed trance.
"AAAAHHHHHH!"
Shouting a chaotic yet desperate battle cry, they charged forward together.
They surrounded the struggling beast, plunging their iron shortswords awkwardly but effectively into the trapped monster until it stopped moving completely.
As the beasts died in the mud, Silas’s internal interface violently roared to life.

Because three entirely different strike teams were actively engaging targets across multiple miles of the Umbral Basin, Silas’s vision became a highly addictive waterfall of pristine blue holographic text.
[Vassal Tamsin has slain a Tier 2 Acid-Crawler. +2 UP]
[Vassal Brida has slain a Tier 1 Iron-Boar. +0.5 UP]
[Vassal Brida has slain a Tier 1 Iron-Boar. +0.5 UP]
[Vassal Aeliana has slain a Tier 1 Mud-Hound. +0.5 UP]
[Vassal Rowena has assisted in a kill. +0.5 UP]
The notifications scrolled endlessly down his peripheral vision, creating a constant pulse of energy entering his Gold Core.
He was sitting securely at the center of a rapidly expanding web of coordinated violence with his upgrade wealth inflating by the second.
The adrenaline of managing a multi-front war was truly amazing.
’I wonder how the other girls are doing...’
Miles away, deep within the jagged, highly treacherous, completely flooded northern ridges, Tamsin wiped a thick smear of mud and freezing rainwater from her sharp eyes.

The Level 10 Wilderness Huntress was crouched extremely low to the wet ground, her twin heavy iron daggers drawn and resting comfortably in her hands. Behind her, a mixed squad of five veteran Shieldmaidens and five wide-eyed newbies mirrored her stealthy stance, using the heavy rotting trunks of the massive Ironwood trees for cover against the rain.
Tamsin’s heart hammered heavily against her ribs.
’I will do it...’
She was fiercely determined.

She had seen the way Silas looked at the S-Rank Chef, and while she understood the logistical necessity of Kaelia keeping them fed, Tamsin wanted to prove that the Vanguard’s undeniable value lay in the mud and the blood.
She wanted to return to the Blessed Land with the highest, most devastating kill count of the entire deployment as she wanted her Lord’s undivided, proud praise.
"The tracks end here..." Tamsin whispered.𝘧𝓇ℯ𝑒𝓌𝑒𝑏𝓃𝘰𝘷𝘦𝘭.𝒸ℴ𝓂
She stared intently at a deep unnatural groove carved directly into the muddy earth.
It looked like something massive had been dragged through the slop, leaving a trail of corrosive, sizzling green slime in its wake that actively killed the weeds.
The rain hammered loudly against the dead leaves above them, completely masking any ambient noise in the forest.
Suddenly, the refined magically enhanced sensory perception Tamsin had gained from her Level 10 ascension screamed a massive, undeniable warning directly into her brain.
The hair on the back of her neck stood up. The ground wasn’t just muddy... It was actively vibrating beneath their boots.
"Shields up!" Tamsin roared, spinning around and throwing her arm out. "Brace for impact!"
The earth directly beneath the squad’s boots violently erupted.
It wasn’t a small ambush.
A horrific horde of over fifty Tier 2 Acid-Crawlers exploded simultaneously from the subterranean mud, completely surrounding them in a ring of clicking mandibles.
The beasts were terrifying... eight-foot-long, heavily armored centipedes with dozens of razor-sharp legs designed to dig through bedrock.
Their massive, clacking mandibles dripped heavily with a foul, venomous, sizzling green fluid that actively melted the dead grass upon contact.
The overwhelming volume and suddenness of the horde instantly shattered the squad’s pristine formation.
"Hold the line!" Gunnhild bellowed, slamming her heavy iron shield into the mud to block a lunging crawler.
The beast’s massive mandibles clamped hard onto the metal, the dripping acid aggressively eating into the iron with a loud hiss.
Chaos descended violently upon the northern ridge.

The veterans fought fiercely, hacking at the heavily armored overlapping segments of the crawlers since they knew the amount of force monsters in the Umbral Basin needed to cave and as for the newbies, their iron swords sparked harmlessly against the thick chitin plates.
Tamsin was a blur of motion.

She didn’t rely on brute force; she relied on precision... Tasmin dove under the snapping mandibles of a massive crawler, driving her twin iron daggers directly upward into the soft, unarmored underbelly of the beast.
SKREEEEE!
The Acid-Crawler shrieked, thrashing wildly as Tamsin ripped her blades free, spilling pale green guts onto the mud.
She rolled smoothly back to her feet, ducking under a sweeping tail strike from another monster.
Tasmin planted her boot on a tree root, launching herself into the air, and brought both daggers down into the exact gap between the crawler’s armored neck plates.
STAB!
The beast collapsed instantly.
She moved like a shadow in the rain.
Left, right, parry, thrust!
Tasmin slaughtered five, then ten of the beasts, her daggers dripping with venomous blood.

She slid through the mud, evading the snapping jaws, targeting only the vulnerable joints that connected their dozens of legs to their bodies but as she ripped her dagger out of her fifteenth kill, a heavy spray of corrosive green acid rained down from a thrashing beast above her.
A splash caught her right shoulder.
The boiled leather of her armor hissed violently, melting away in an instant.
A sharp, burning pain flared across her skin as the acid bit into her flesh, trying to dissolve the muscle.
"Mmmmm..."
It hurt.
Tamsin gritted her teeth, ignoring the agonizing sting. It wasn’t a lethal wound, but it burned like hellfire.
She kicked the dead crawler away and spun to engage the next wave, but as her sharp eyes swept across the battlefield, she caught the devastating reality of the skirmish.
They were completely overwhelmed...
Tamsin was racking up kills, but there were simply too many of them.
For every crawler she as well as the others killed, three more erupted from the mud to take its place.
The overwhelming volume of the horde was suffocating.
The five rookies were panicking, backing up into each other, their iron swords trembling as the massive centipedes completely encircled them.
Gunnhild’s shield was rapidly melting under the continuous assault of the acid, the structural integrity failing.
Another veteran Shieldmaiden had been knocked to the ground, desperately holding off snapping mandibles with the wooden shaft of her spear, her arms shaking from the exertion.
They were going to be eaten alive in the mud if the lines completely broke...

’Not today,’ Tamsin thought, her eyes narrowing as she kicked a lunging crawler directly in its snapping jaws, sending it tumbling back into the slop. ’I will not lose a single girl on my watch... I will not bring casualties back to the Lord...’
Tamsin raised her left hand. Glowing beneath the thick layer of mud and freezing rainwater was the complex, geometric emerald mark Eluned had kissed onto her skin before they departed.
With a roar of unyielding, desperate defiance, Tamsin slammed her right palm directly against the glowing rune.
She forcefully injected a massive surge of her own gathered mana directly into the divine tether.
[Aura of Genesis (Emulated) Activated.]
The response was magnificent.

A roaring tidal wave of brilliant, pure emerald light erupted violently from Tamsin’s hand, violently pushing back the gray gloom of the monsoon and momentarily blinding the surrounding Acid-Crawlers.
The SSS-Rank nature magic flooded the entire battlefield.

The agonizing, melting fire on Tamsin’s shoulder was instantly, completely snuffed out as the divine energy neutralized the venomous acid, weaving her burned skin back together in a fraction of a second until not even a scar remained.
But the aura didn’t just heal her minor burn. The emerald light washed over the exhausted, terrified squad...
It flooded their veins with an overflowing reservoir of endless divine stamina.
The fear instantly evaporated from the rookies’ eyes, replaced by a surge of overwhelming adrenaline.
Gunnhild let out a massive, booming laugh as her muscles bulged with fresh, unyielding power, throwing her melting shield aside and gripping her broadsword with both hands.
Tamsin sucked in a massive breath of cold air, her eyes snapping open, glowing with a small emerald hue from the blessing.
Her fatigue was entirely gone.
"Push them back!" Tamsin roared, her survivalist instincts sharpening into a terrifying razor’s edge.
She gripped her twin daggers, launching herself back into the horde. "Slaughter every single one of them!"
But before she could take a single step, the bruised-purple sky directly above the northern ridge violently tore open.
The deafening relentless howl of the monsoon rain was momentarily overpowered by the terrifying high-pitched shriek of hyper-compressed mana tearing through the atmosphere.
The sheer volume of the sound was agonizing... a pressure that vibrated through the teeth and bones of every living creature on the ridge.
Miles away, standing safely atop the towering, rune-carved observation deck of the Blood-Iron Watchtower, Eluned and Fenna had not been idle.
They had been meticulously tracking the Vanguard’s localized mana signatures through the highly advanced, magically-assisted scopes mounted on the heavy ballistae.
The scopes, fueled by the S-Rank Goddess’s nature mana and Fenna’s peerless archery calculations, allowed them to pierce through the heavy rain and the dense canopy of the dead forest.

When they saw Tamsin’s distinct emerald signature... the beacon of the Genesis Rune became completely enveloped by a massive swarm of hostile crawler signatures, they didn’t wait for a desperate distress signal.
They didn’t ask for permission to engage, knowing that a delay of even three seconds would result in casualties.
KRA-THOOM! KRA-THOOM! KRA-THOOM!
Three massive, devastating bolts of pure, concentrated blue artillery screamed down from the heavens like catastrophic orbital strikes.

The sheer friction of the heavy projectiles moving through the atmosphere violently vaporized the freezing rain in their path, leaving three massive, perfectly straight trails of blinding white steam hanging in the gray sky.
The heavy, mythril-tipped ballista bolts slammed directly into the absolute densest clusters of the Acid-Crawler horde surrounding Tamsin’s squad.
BOOM! BOOM! BOOM!
The impacts were utterly apocalyptic.
The saturated, highly unstable mud violently cratered under the massive force, sending massive, rippling shockwaves tearing through the forest floor.

The concussive blasts were so overwhelmingly powerful that several nearby petrified Ironwood trees were instantly uprooted, their massive rotting trunks snapping like dry twigs and crashing heavily into the slop.
Dozens of the heavy, armored centipedes were instantly vaporized at the epicenter of the strikes.
The incredibly dense, magically forged artillery simply erased their biology from existence.
Those caught in the outer blast radius were violently blown into highly fragmented chunks of burning chitin, severed razor-legs, and sizzling green fluid that rained down harmlessly across the ridge.
Fenna’s peerless calculation was absolute.

The massive explosions completely bypassed the Vanguard’s defensive perimeter... Not a single piece of shrapnel or drop of highly corrosive acid touched the cowering rookies or the battered veterans as the destruction was entirely restricted to the enemy lines.
’Like I said... they can operate the Watchtower much better than I can.’ Tasmin thought.
The overwhelming ambush was instantly broken.
The horde’s terrifying numbers, previously suffocating the squad from all sides, were violently reduced to a fraction of their strength in less than three seconds of overwhelming artillery fire.
Tamsin stood completely unharmed in the exact center of the smoking, steaming, highly acidic craters.
The extreme heat of the ballista strikes had temporarily boiled the mud around her boots, baking the earth into hard, cracked clay.
She was bathed in the warm emerald light of the Genesis Rune radiating from her fist as her twin daggers gripped tightly in her calloused hands.
Tasmin looked up at the bruising gray sky, tracing the lingering trails of steam leading back to the Blessed Land.
A fierce unhinged grin spread across her mud-splattered face.
’Yes that was from our Territory...’
The overwhelming dominance of their territory’s firepower sent an intoxicating rush of adrenaline straight into her brain.
They were not fighting a desperate battle at all... they were the executioners of the Umbral Basin.
Tasmin turned rapidly to her squad.
The five veteran Shieldmaidens and the five newly summoned rookies were staring at her, staring at the massive smoking craters, and staring at the raining bug parts in reverence.
Their iron swords were trembling, but not from fear of the monsters... rather from the incomprehensible awe of the firepower their Sovereign commanded.
"The Watchtower has our backs!" Tamsin roared.

The emerald light from her hand flared, washing over her squad and purging the last remnants of their terror. "Do not let a single one of these surviving beasts escape into the mud! We clear this ridge! Charge!"

The overwhelming volume and suddenness of the horde instantly shattered the squad’s pristine formation.

chapters.title: Chapter 34: Going To War [III]
paragraphs: Empowered by the overwhelming divine stamina still actively radiating from their captain’s blessing, the five veterans and the five terrified rookies let out a unified, deafening, highly aggressive battle cry.
"RAAHHHHHH!"
The paralyzing fear of the Unknown Zone was entirely replaced by the intoxicating thrill of overwhelming superiority.
The rookies, who only moments ago had been backing away in tears, felt the divine energy harden their muscles and sharpen their vision.
They charged violently forward as a singlE cohesive unit.
They didn’t break rank... instead they moved with the pack-hunting synchronicity Tamsin had drilled into them.
Their heavy iron blades rose and fell in a brutal, highly coordinated counter-offensive.
They ruthlessly butchered the disoriented, terrified remnants of the Acid-Crawler horde before the massive insects could burrow back into the safety of the earth.
"That’s what I like to see!"

Gunnhild led the vanguard, her heavy broadsword severing heads with singular, brutal chops, while the rookies followed closely behind, driving their shortswords into the exposed unarmored underbellies of the thrashing centipedes.
Tamsin moved through the chaos like a ghost, her daggers flawlessly severing the neural clusters of any crawler that attempted to spit acid at her girls.
WHOOSH! WHOOSH! WHOOSH!
It wasn’t a fight anymore like it had been... it was a completely one-sided extermination.
Directly across the sprawling territory, miles away deep within the eastern thickets, the environment was entirely different.𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝚠𝕖𝐛𝗻𝗼𝐯𝕖𝚕.𝚌𝗼𝗺
"Bring it on you pungent beasts!"
The terrain here was relatively flat, completely lacking the treacherous vertical drops of the ravines or the deep unstable sinkholes of the north.

But the heavy monsoon rain had turned the dense overgrown brush into a highly restrictive, nearly impassable maze of petrified thorny vines and thick, sucking mud that aggressively gripped at their iron-plated boots.
Visibility was restricted to less than thirty feet, completely obscured by the gray rain and the dense, twisting gray foliage.
Brida didn’t rely on agility to navigate the thickets, and she certainly didn’t rely on stealth to avoid the local predators.
The Level 11 Shieldmaiden stood firmly at the front of an unyielding wall of solid iron.
Behind her, ten highly experienced veteran Shieldmaidens and five heavily armored infantry rookies stood shoulder-to-shoulder with their breathing synchronized and their muscles locked.

Their massive, thick iron tower shields were heavily, perfectly overlapped, the reinforced edges locking together to form a flawless turtle-shell formation that completely blocked the narrow, muddy path through the thorns.

"Anchor your boots!" Brida barked with her deep commanding voice booming easily over the relentless roar of the rain. "Drop your center of gravity! Dig your heels straight into the bedrock beneath the slop! Do not let the mud steal your balance! You are the wall!"
Charging blindly and aggressively through the dense thickets directly toward their entrenched formation was a massive, highly agitated pack of mutated, Tier 2 Iron-Boars.
The beasts were massive, heavily muscled aggressive swine that easily weighed four hundred pounds apiece.
Thick, jagged metallic tusks, forged entirely from naturally ingested iron ore found in the basin’s roots, protruded dangerously from their heavy frothing jaws.
They didn’t possess complex, highly coordinated pack tactics like the Umbral Hounds... rather they operated entirely on raw overwhelming physical momentum.
They were monstrous battering rams, specifically designed by the corruptive ecosystem to completely shatter enemy lines and trample the survivors into the dirt.
"Brace!" Brida ordered, slamming the heavy spiked bottom of her own massive shield deeply into the mud, anchoring her stance with Level 11 vitality.
The massive pack of boars slammed headfirst, entirely at full speed, directly into the Vanguard’s shield wall.
BOOOOOOOMM!!!!
The loud booming sound of dense bone and jagged metallic tusk crashing violently against solid iron echoed sharply through the eastern thicket like a series of rapid anvil strikes.

The five rookies, positioned strategically in the absolute center of the defensive line where the overlapping shields provided the most structural support, grunted heavily under the immense strain in their arms.
Their iron-plated boots slid back a dangerous terrifying inch in the slop under the massive concentrated physical pressure of the charge.

The force threatened to dislocate their shoulders with their forearms burning as the iron boars wildly thrashed and continuously rammed their tusks against the metal in a frenzied attempt to break through but the iron wall did not break.
Brida had spent her entire mornings in the courtyard drilling these women until their muscles bled, their lungs burned, and their arms were completely numb.
She also taught these new recruits some stuff on their way here so they knew exactly how to physically distribute the crushing weight of a massive charge evenly across the interlocked shields.
They utilized their newly enhanced Level 3 vitality, feeding their raw stamina directly into their stances to perfectly absorb the shock.

"Hold the line!" Brida commanded, her own [ Steel Aegis] actively glowing with an unyielding blue light, easily absorbing the bone-shattering impact of the largest, heaviest lead boar without her even flinching. "Thrust on my mark! Do not break the overlap! Keep your shields locked!"

The boars squealed wildly in frenzied frustration with their heavy hooves kicking up massive sprays of muddy water as they rapidly backed up in the slop to aggressively charge the unyielding metal wall again.
"Mark!" Brida roared.
In perfect terrifying unison, the fifteen Shieldmaidens briefly, precisely angled their massive shields outward by a mere fraction of an inch.
It was just enough to create a lethal opening without compromising the structural integrity of the phalanx.
They drove their heavy, razor-sharp iron shortswords directly through the narrow carefully calculated gaps in the defensive formation.
WHOOOOOOSHHHHHH!
They didn’t swing wildly... instead they thrust with a singular intent.
They plunged the heavy blades deeply into the exposed vulnerable throats and soft unarmored underbellies of the charging beasts exactly as the boars threw their weight forward.
SHLK! SHLK! SHLK!
The synchronized lethal execution dropped half the massive pack in a single devastating heartbeat.
The heavy iron blades pierced internal organs, severed major arteries, and instantly halted the monsters’ momentum.
Thick black blood poured heavily from the fatal wounds, spilling violently into the mud and instantly washing away in the relentless rain.
The dying boars collapsed against the shields, their heavy bodies sliding down the iron faceplates and piling up in front of the Vanguard’s boots.
"Recover! Brace!" Brida shouted immediately, not allowing her squad a single second to celebrate or relax their muscles.

The Shieldmaidens violently, flawlessly reset the impenetrable iron wall, locking the edges of their shields back together before the remaining confused boars could attempt to exploit the momentary offensive openings.
It wasn’t a flashy, highly destructive, visually spectacular display of cosmic magic like Aeliana’s beams or Rowena’s gravity wells...
It completely lacked the chaotic desperate adrenaline of Tamsin’s brawl in the north... That was because it wasn’t meant to be.
It was a slow and terrifying meat grinder.
Brida’s heavy infantry squad operated like a singular emotionless machine of war.
They flawlessly crushed the enemy’s momentum against their shields, absorbed their energy without yielding an inch of ground, and bled them entirely dry in the mud without taking a single casualty.
They repeated the brutal cycle.
Brace... Absorb... Mark... Thrust... Recover!
As the very last mutated Iron-Boar finally fell, choking heavily on its own blood in the slop with three iron shortswords buried in its chest, Brida didn’t immediately lower her massive shield.
Her highly alert eyes scanned the dense thorny thicket with her senses hyper-focused on the shadows between the petrified trees, ensuring nothing else was preparing to charge from the darkness.

Only when the heavy drum of the freezing rain hitting the mud was the only sound left echoing in the woods did she finally stand up straight, lowering the heavy iron shield to rest against her greaves.
"Clear!" Brida announced, turning her head to look at her squad.
The five rookies were panting heavily with their chests heaving against their iron breastplates.
Their arms were visibly trembling from the repeated concussive weight of the charges with the lactic acid burning in their muscles but their eyes were shining bright with immense pride.
They had stared down a massive, charging horde of monsters in the pouring rain, and they had held the Vanguard line. They had not broken.
They were officially soldiers of the Blessed Land.

"Harvest the iron tusks for now," Brida ordered smoothly, highly satisfied with their flawless performance. "Our Lord needs his points to build our home, and we need to get more of it. We keep moving until the absolute quota is met. Leave the meat for now; it is entirely too tough to transport in this weather."
As her squad quickly moved to butcher the fallen boars, leveraging their shortswords to pry the valuable iron tusks from the heavy jaws, Brida looked up at the bruising gray sky.
A deeply satisfied smirk touched her scarred lips with the heavy rain washing the sweat from her brow.
’What an amazing day... Should I ask my Lord to reward me?’

She liked it... The multi-front war was aggressively pushing the Vanguard to its absolute physical limits, forcing them to operate independently without Silas actively holding their hands but they were not breaking under the immense pressure.
They were violently and rapidly evolving into a self-sustaining military force.

Every single drop of monster blood spilled in the freezing mud was a solid brick laid perfectly in the foundation of the empire Silas was building and they would gladly drag this entire necrotic rotting basin to its knees if he ordered it.
The flooded western quarry was a treacherous claustrophobic nightmare of jagged black stone and rapidly rising murky brown water.
The heavy monsoon rain continued to hammer down relentlessly against the Umbral Basin, rapidly filling the massive uneven crater.

The highly efficient slaughter of the initial Tier 1 Mud-Hound pack had painted the flooded basin in thick, swirling ribbons of corrosive black blood but the heavy downpour was already aggressively washing the evidence of the Vanguard’s efficiency away, heavily diluting the gore and dragging it down into the churning mud at the bottom of the sinkhole.
Silas stood near the highly precarious edge of a submerged steep drop-off.
His boots were anchored firmly and flawlessly against a slick uneven slab of solid bedrock that jutted out just slightly above the rising waterline.
’I’ve gotten quite a lot of UP but we need more...’
He slowly lowered his Umbral-Forged Mythril Blade, allowing the freezing rain to wash the remaining sizzling gore from the dark-purple metal.
A steady trickle of foundational energy from his Mythic Gold Core continued to radiate steadily across his skin.

The thermal pocket violently vaporized the freezing raindrops the moment they touched his black combat robes, completely nullifying the environmental hazard and enveloping his broad shoulders in an intimidating hissing shroud of steam.
He looked over his shoulder with his blue eyes assessing the physical and mental condition of his squad.
Rowena stood a few feet away on a neighboring rock outcropping.
Her breathing was perfectly steady, her blue eyes actively scanning the dark rain-soaked horizon as her heavy wooden staff pulsed softly with residual gravity magic.
Aeliana stood firmly beside her.
The Royal Elven Arcanist was displaying a terrifyingly cold composure that completely erased the embarrassing memory of her frantic breakdown in the bat cavern.

She held her ground perfectly on the slippery rocks, her green eyes scanning the murky water for any signs of movement and her mana pathways primed and ready to unleash another devastating volley of starlight at a moment’s notice.
Behind the two elite spellcasters, the five newly summoned recruits were in medium shape.
The rookies were leaning heavily against their iron shortswords, their chests heaving violently as they desperately tried to pull oxygen into their burning lungs.
They were utterly soaked to the bone, their thin leather armor entirely caked in freezing mud.

The massive rush of adrenaline from surviving their first true chaotic brawl in the Unknown Zone was rapidly wearing off, leaving their muscles weak and their bodies shivering violently in the biting wind.

"Form up to keep yourselves warm!" Silas commanded with a small smile. "You girls did very well but do not let the cold settle into your joints... Keep your blood moving! Check your gear, confirm your blades are secure, and prepare to advance!"
Silas then sighed as he rubbed the back of his head.
"I’m sorry for dragging you new girls out here." He said, he had wanted them to see the front lines and so far they had gained quite some levels.
"My Lord! We are your soldiers!" One of them puffed up with a blush on her cheeks. "It’s our duty and you’re really amazing!"
The girls agreed with her immediately, including Rowena and Aeliana.

sentences.text: Empowered by the overwhelming divine stamina still actively radiating from their captain’s blessing, the five veterans and the five terrified rookies let out a unified, deafening, highly aggressive battle cry.
"RAAHHHHHH!"
The paralyzing fear of the Unknown Zone was entirely replaced by the intoxicating thrill of overwhelming superiority.
The rookies, who only moments ago had been backing away in tears, felt the divine energy harden their muscles and sharpen their vision.
They charged violently forward as a singlE cohesive unit.
They didn’t break rank... instead they moved with the pack-hunting synchronicity Tamsin had drilled into them.
Their heavy iron blades rose and fell in a brutal, highly coordinated counter-offensive.
They ruthlessly butchered the disoriented, terrified remnants of the Acid-Crawler horde before the massive insects could burrow back into the safety of the earth.
"That’s what I like to see!"

Gunnhild led the vanguard, her heavy broadsword severing heads with singular, brutal chops, while the rookies followed closely behind, driving their shortswords into the exposed unarmored underbellies of the thrashing centipedes.
Tamsin moved through the chaos like a ghost, her daggers flawlessly severing the neural clusters of any crawler that attempted to spit acid at her girls.
WHOOSH!
WHOOSH!
WHOOSH!
It wasn’t a fight anymore like it had been... it was a completely one-sided extermination.
Directly across the sprawling territory, miles away deep within the eastern thickets, the environment was entirely different.𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝚠𝕖𝐛𝗻𝗼𝐯𝕖𝚕.𝚌𝗼𝗺
"Bring it on you pungent beasts!"
The terrain here was relatively flat, completely lacking the treacherous vertical drops of the ravines or the deep unstable sinkholes of the north.

But the heavy monsoon rain had turned the dense overgrown brush into a highly restrictive, nearly impassable maze of petrified thorny vines and thick, sucking mud that aggressively gripped at their iron-plated boots.
Visibility was restricted to less than thirty feet, completely obscured by the gray rain and the dense, twisting gray foliage.
Brida didn’t rely on agility to navigate the thickets, and she certainly didn’t rely on stealth to avoid the local predators.
The Level 11 Shieldmaiden stood firmly at the front of an unyielding wall of solid iron.
Behind her, ten highly experienced veteran Shieldmaidens and five heavily armored infantry rookies stood shoulder-to-shoulder with their breathing synchronized and their muscles locked.

Their massive, thick iron tower shields were heavily, perfectly overlapped, the reinforced edges locking together to form a flawless turtle-shell formation that completely blocked the narrow, muddy path through the thorns.
"Anchor your boots!" Brida barked with her deep commanding voice booming easily over the relentless roar of the rain.
"Drop your center of gravity!
Dig your heels straight into the bedrock beneath the slop!
Do not let the mud steal your balance!
You are the wall!"
Charging blindly and aggressively through the dense thickets directly toward their entrenched formation was a massive, highly agitated pack of mutated, Tier 2 Iron-Boars.
The beasts were massive, heavily muscled aggressive swine that easily weighed four hundred pounds apiece.
Thick, jagged metallic tusks, forged entirely from naturally ingested iron ore found in the basin’s roots, protruded dangerously from their heavy frothing jaws.
They didn’t possess complex, highly coordinated pack tactics like the Umbral Hounds... rather they operated entirely on raw overwhelming physical momentum.
They were monstrous battering rams, specifically designed by the corruptive ecosystem to completely shatter enemy lines and trample the survivors into the dirt.
"Brace!" Brida ordered, slamming the heavy spiked bottom of her own massive shield deeply into the mud, anchoring her stance with Level 11 vitality.
The massive pack of boars slammed headfirst, entirely at full speed, directly into the Vanguard’s shield wall.
BOOOOOOOMM!!!!
The loud booming sound of dense bone and jagged metallic tusk crashing violently against solid iron echoed sharply through the eastern thicket like a series of rapid anvil strikes.

The five rookies, positioned strategically in the absolute center of the defensive line where the overlapping shields provided the most structural support, grunted heavily under the immense strain in their arms.
Their iron-plated boots slid back a dangerous terrifying inch in the slop under the massive concentrated physical pressure of the charge.

The force threatened to dislocate their shoulders with their forearms burning as the iron boars wildly thrashed and continuously rammed their tusks against the metal in a frenzied attempt to break through but the iron wall did not break.
Brida had spent her entire mornings in the courtyard drilling these women until their muscles bled, their lungs burned, and their arms were completely numb.
She also taught these new recruits some stuff on their way here so they knew exactly how to physically distribute the crushing weight of a massive charge evenly across the interlocked shields.
They utilized their newly enhanced Level 3 vitality, feeding their raw stamina directly into their stances to perfectly absorb the shock.

"Hold the line!" Brida commanded, her own [ Steel Aegis] actively glowing with an unyielding blue light, easily absorbing the bone-shattering impact of the largest, heaviest lead boar without her even flinching.
"Thrust on my mark!
Do not break the overlap!
Keep your shields locked!"

The boars squealed wildly in frenzied frustration with their heavy hooves kicking up massive sprays of muddy water as they rapidly backed up in the slop to aggressively charge the unyielding metal wall again.
"Mark!" Brida roared.
In perfect terrifying unison, the fifteen Shieldmaidens briefly, precisely angled their massive shields outward by a mere fraction of an inch.
It was just enough to create a lethal opening without compromising the structural integrity of the phalanx.
They drove their heavy, razor-sharp iron shortswords directly through the narrow carefully calculated gaps in the defensive formation.
WHOOOOOOSHHHHHH!
They didn’t swing wildly... instead they thrust with a singular intent.
They plunged the heavy blades deeply into the exposed vulnerable throats and soft unarmored underbellies of the charging beasts exactly as the boars threw their weight forward.
SHLK!
SHLK!
SHLK!
The synchronized lethal execution dropped half the massive pack in a single devastating heartbeat.
The heavy iron blades pierced internal organs, severed major arteries, and instantly halted the monsters’ momentum.
Thick black blood poured heavily from the fatal wounds, spilling violently into the mud and instantly washing away in the relentless rain.
The dying boars collapsed against the shields, their heavy bodies sliding down the iron faceplates and piling up in front of the Vanguard’s boots.
"Recover!
Brace!" Brida shouted immediately, not allowing her squad a single second to celebrate or relax their muscles.

The Shieldmaidens violently, flawlessly reset the impenetrable iron wall, locking the edges of their shields back together before the remaining confused boars could attempt to exploit the momentary offensive openings.
It wasn’t a flashy, highly destructive, visually spectacular display of cosmic magic like Aeliana’s beams or Rowena’s gravity wells...
It completely lacked the chaotic desperate adrenaline of Tamsin’s brawl in the north...
That was because it wasn’t meant to be.
It was a slow and terrifying meat grinder.
Brida’s heavy infantry squad operated like a singular emotionless machine of war.
They flawlessly crushed the enemy’s momentum against their shields, absorbed their energy without yielding an inch of ground, and bled them entirely dry in the mud without taking a single casualty.
They repeated the brutal cycle.
Brace...
Absorb...
Mark...
Thrust...
Recover!
As the very last mutated Iron-Boar finally fell, choking heavily on its own blood in the slop with three iron shortswords buried in its chest, Brida didn’t immediately lower her massive shield.
Her highly alert eyes scanned the dense thorny thicket with her senses hyper-focused on the shadows between the petrified trees, ensuring nothing else was preparing to charge from the darkness.

Only when the heavy drum of the freezing rain hitting the mud was the only sound left echoing in the woods did she finally stand up straight, lowering the heavy iron shield to rest against her greaves.
"Clear!" Brida announced, turning her head to look at her squad.
The five rookies were panting heavily with their chests heaving against their iron breastplates.
Their arms were visibly trembling from the repeated concussive weight of the charges with the lactic acid burning in their muscles but their eyes were shining bright with immense pride.
They had stared down a massive, charging horde of monsters in the pouring rain, and they had held the Vanguard line.
They had not broken.
They were officially soldiers of the Blessed Land.
"Harvest the iron tusks for now," Brida ordered smoothly, highly satisfied with their flawless performance.
"Our Lord needs his points to build our home, and we need to get more of it.
We keep moving until the absolute quota is met.
Leave the meat for now; it is entirely too tough to transport in this weather."
As her squad quickly moved to butcher the fallen boars, leveraging their shortswords to pry the valuable iron tusks from the heavy jaws, Brida looked up at the bruising gray sky.
A deeply satisfied smirk touched her scarred lips with the heavy rain washing the sweat from her brow.
’What an amazing day...
Should I ask my Lord to reward me?’
She liked it...

The multi-front war was aggressively pushing the Vanguard to its absolute physical limits, forcing them to operate independently without Silas actively holding their hands but they were not breaking under the immense pressure.
They were violently and rapidly evolving into a self-sustaining military force.

Every single drop of monster blood spilled in the freezing mud was a solid brick laid perfectly in the foundation of the empire Silas was building and they would gladly drag this entire necrotic rotting basin to its knees if he ordered it.
The flooded western quarry was a treacherous claustrophobic nightmare of jagged black stone and rapidly rising murky brown water.
The heavy monsoon rain continued to hammer down relentlessly against the Umbral Basin, rapidly filling the massive uneven crater.

The highly efficient slaughter of the initial Tier 1 Mud-Hound pack had painted the flooded basin in thick, swirling ribbons of corrosive black blood but the heavy downpour was already aggressively washing the evidence of the Vanguard’s efficiency away, heavily diluting the gore and dragging it down into the churning mud at the bottom of the sinkhole.
Silas stood near the highly precarious edge of a submerged steep drop-off.
His boots were anchored firmly and flawlessly against a slick uneven slab of solid bedrock that jutted out just slightly above the rising waterline.
’I’ve gotten quite a lot of UP but we need more...’
He slowly lowered his Umbral-Forged Mythril Blade, allowing the freezing rain to wash the remaining sizzling gore from the dark-purple metal.
A steady trickle of foundational energy from his Mythic Gold Core continued to radiate steadily across his skin.

The thermal pocket violently vaporized the freezing raindrops the moment they touched his black combat robes, completely nullifying the environmental hazard and enveloping his broad shoulders in an intimidating hissing shroud of steam.
He looked over his shoulder with his blue eyes assessing the physical and mental condition of his squad.
Rowena stood a few feet away on a neighboring rock outcropping.
Her breathing was perfectly steady, her blue eyes actively scanning the dark rain-soaked horizon as her heavy wooden staff pulsed softly with residual gravity magic.
Aeliana stood firmly beside her.
The Royal Elven Arcanist was displaying a terrifyingly cold composure that completely erased the embarrassing memory of her frantic breakdown in the bat cavern.

She held her ground perfectly on the slippery rocks, her green eyes scanning the murky water for any signs of movement and her mana pathways primed and ready to unleash another devastating volley of starlight at a moment’s notice.
Behind the two elite spellcasters, the five newly summoned recruits were in medium shape.
The rookies were leaning heavily against their iron shortswords, their chests heaving violently as they desperately tried to pull oxygen into their burning lungs.
They were utterly soaked to the bone, their thin leather armor entirely caked in freezing mud.

The massive rush of adrenaline from surviving their first true chaotic brawl in the Unknown Zone was rapidly wearing off, leaving their muscles weak and their bodies shivering violently in the biting wind.
"Form up to keep yourselves warm!" Silas commanded with a small smile.
"You girls did very well but do not let the cold settle into your joints...
Keep your blood moving!
Check your gear, confirm your blades are secure, and prepare to advance!"
Silas then sighed as he rubbed the back of his head.
"I’m sorry for dragging you new girls out here." He said, he had wanted them to see the front lines and so far they had gained quite some levels.
"My Lord!
We are your soldiers!" One of them puffed up with a blush on her cheeks.
"It’s our duty and you’re really amazing!"
The girls agreed with her immediately, including Rowena and Aeliana.

chapters.title: Chapter 35: Going To War [IV]
paragraphs: "My Lord," Rowena spoke up, taking a cautious step closer to him.
Her heavy blue robes dragged heavily in the muddy water, completely ruined by the slop.
Her delicate brow was deeply furrowed in extreme concern.

"The amount of blood from the hounds has thoroughly saturated the water supply in this crater as the concentration of gore is incredibly high. By all standard survival metrics and basic magical ecology, the scent of the slaughter should have instantly drawn dozens of lesser scavengers from the surrounding ridges to feast."
Silas narrowed his blue eyes, looking out over the dark churning expanse of the flooded quarry.
The gray rain battered the surface of the water, creating a rippling texture that made it impossible to see beneath the surface.
She was entirely correct.
The Umbral Basin was primarily defined by its relentless aggressive hunger.
Every creature in the dark was starving.
A fresh kill site, especially one reeking of heavy black blood and fresh meat, was essentially a blaring dinner bell for every desperate mutation within a five-mile radius.
Scavengers should have been crawling out of the woodwork to fight over the scraps.
Yet, as Silas actively tapped into his core and utilized his highly refined, Gold Core-enhanced sensory perception to sweep the immediate area for hostile mana signatures, he felt absolutely nothing.

There were no chittering insects hiding in the dark rock crevices... There were no secondary packs of hounds howling in the distant, rain-obscured treeline... There wasn’t even the faint scuttling of a bottom-feeder in the shallows...
The entire western crater had fallen into a completely unnatural silence, broken only by the heavy drumming of the rain hitting the water.
It felt very wrong.

’The scavengers aren’t coming...’ Silas realized as his mind pieced the concerning environmental clues together. ’They aren’t ignoring the massive amount of blood in the water... They are probably terrified so they are actively avoiding this specific crater because it already belongs to something else... Something massive probably.’
"Shields up!" Silas roared, instantly snapping his mythril blade back into a highly defensive and dropping his center of gravity. "Fall back to the elevated rocks! Now!"
The booming command hit the squad like a physical blow. Aeliana didn’t ask questions as her discipline was locked in.

She instantly reached out and grabbed the nearest, heavily shivering rookie by the collar of her iron breastplate, forcefully dragging the exhausted girl backward toward the jagged black spires jutting higher out of the mud.
Before the rest of the highly disoriented rookies could scramble to the safety of higher ground, the flooded quarry violently responded to their presence.
It started as a deep loud subterranean tremor.
The violent vibration originated directly beneath the darkest deepest section of the flooded basin, exactly where they had just been standing mere moments ago.
The ancient bedrock groaned with a deafening, echoing crunch that violently rattled the Vanguard’s teeth inside their skulls.
The murky blood-stained water in the center of the crater began to violently churn.
It rapidly expanded, rotating into a massive dangerous whirlpool that aggressively sucked the floating corpses of the dead Mud-Hounds down into the pitch-black depths.

"Brace yourselves!" Rowena shouted, slamming her staff deep into the rock to anchor her footing as a powerful tidal wave of muddy water washed aggressively over their boots, nearly sweeping the remaining off-balance rookies away.
Bursting violently from the absolute center of the swirling chaotic vortex was the undisputed apex predator of the western ridges.
[Target Analyzed: Mire-Drake Matriarch (Tier 3 Boss)]
[Warning: Extreme seismic manipulation detected.]
The beast was absolutely colossal.
It easily rivaled the size of a heavy military siege wagon, measuring a terrifying eighty feet from its heavily armored, crocodilian snout to the tip of its jagged whip-like tail.
Its anatomical structure resembled a massive corrupted alligator but its overarching biology had heavily mutated to perfectly dominate the muddy flooded terrain of the basin.
Its dark green slippery scales were completely reinforced by massive compressed plates of magically infused stone.

The bedrock armor completely covered its spine, its broad shoulders, and its massive skull, transforming the beast into an incredibly dense living fortress that looked entirely immune to standard iron weaponry.
The Mire-Drake Matriarch did not immediately blindly attack the squad.
She dragged her colossal, heavy torso aggressively onto a massive slab of submerged rock, raising her heavily armored head toward the bruising gray sky.
The weight of her body visibly crushed the stone beneath her claws.
The Matriarch unhinged her massive, cavernous jaws and let out a roar.
"RAHHHHHHHHHH!!"
The roar was a highly concentrated powerful concussive shockwave of atmospheric pressure.

The warping distortion wave violently tore through the heavy rain, vaporizing the falling water instantly before slamming directly into the Vanguard’s formation with the physical force of a swinging battering ram.
The impact of the sonic sound wave was staggering.
Silas braced his heavy boots, his Gold Core flaring brightly to flawlessly anchor his center of gravity against the bedrock.
The concussive force washed over him, completely unbothered by the immense pressure but the mortal heavy infantry girls standing behind him were completely overwhelmed.
The five rookies screamed as the concussive force violently picked them up off their feet and threw them backward off the slick elevated rocks.
Their heavy boots entirely lost traction on the wet stone, and they tumbled heavily, crashing down into the deep churning slop of the lower basin with a series of heavy splashes.
"Get up!" Aeliana commanded, fighting through the painful, disorienting ringing in her pointed ears.

She scrambled frantically to the edge of the rocks, dropping to her knees and reaching her pale hand down toward the struggling newbies thrashing in the water below But the Tier 3 Boss was not a mindless raging brute.
She possessed a terrifying cunning born of centuries of survival at the top of the Umbral Basin’s food chain.
The Matriarch didn’t blindly charge the armed dangerous Sovereign standing perfectly balanced on the high ground.

She recognized the threat he posed. Instead, her glowing, sickly-yellow, entirely reptilian eyes locked directly onto the five panicked rookies who represented the scattered disoriented prey struggling helplessly in the mud.
The massive beast slammed her heavily armored, boulder-sized front claws directly into the flooded earth with bone-shattering force.
[Warning: Hostile Terrain Manipulation Activated.]
The muddy water directly beneath the five rookies violently shuddered.

The Matriarch actively, aggressively channeled her incredibly dense, earth-aligned magical energy directly into the flooded crater. The standard, slippery mud instantly pressurized. The spell turned the entire lower basin into a massive, violently swirling vortex of highly restrictive, incredibly deep magical quicksand.
The rookies shrieked in terror as the solid ground entirely vanished beneath them.

"I’m stuck! I can’t move my legs!" one of the girls cried out, dropping her heavy iron shortsword into the slop in a blind panic as the highly pressurized mud instantly sucked her boots down past her ankles.
The more they struggled to pull their legs free, the faster the magical quicksand consumed them, utilizing their own energy against them.

Within three terrifying seconds, the thick mud had aggressively swallowed their shins, actively pulling them deeper into the earth under the crushing, undeniable weight of their own heavy iron breastplates.
The trap was flawlessly executed, completely immobilizing the absolute weakest links in the formation and leaving them entirely defenseless in the open for the Matriarch to devour at her leisure.
"Rowena, pull them out!" Silas ordered with his voice cracking like a whip.

He immediately stepped off the safety of the rocks and splashed heavily down into the shallows, his superheated mythril blade raised high, intending to draw the Matriarch’s attention before she could snap her jaws around the trapped girls.

"I can’t!" Rowena yelled back, her knuckles turning entirely white around her wooden staff with her face pale with absolute dread as she frantically calculated the magical physics. "If I use a Gravity Well to pull them out of the quicksand, the multiplied gravitational pressure required to break the suction will instantly, violently crush their legs!"
The Matriarch let out a low, deeply satisfied rumble that vibrated through the dense mud, rattling the loose jagged black stones at the perilous edge of the flooded quarry.
RRRRRRRUMBLLLLLE!
It was a physical force that resonated in the chest cavities of the Vanguard, vibrating through the iron plates of their armor and rattling their teeth.
Seeing her prey hopelessly, perfectly pinned in the swirling vortex of her magical quicksand, the colossal beast coiled her massive armored crocodilian legs beneath her.
The thick, magically infused stone plates that acted as her natural armor scraped and ground against the submerged bedrock with a sickening scraping noise.

She prepared to launch her entire eighty-foot, siege-wagon-sized body directly across the span of the crater with her unhinged jaws ready to consume the five trapped, screaming girls in a single devastating blood-soaked bite.
Aeliana stared at the massive beast, her refined mind running complex arcane calculations in a fraction of a heartbeat.
She could feel the heavy density of the beast’s earth magic anchoring the slop, turning the natural terrain into a deadly pressurized weapon.

’The mud is actively pressurized by superior earth magic...’ Aeliana analyzed, her green eyes glowed with fierce determination as the freezing monsoon rain plastered her pristine silver hair directly to her pale cheeks. ’I cannot out-muscle a Tier 3 Boss’s elemental control since her raw output dwarfs mine by several orders of magnitude. The density of her mana is simply too vast but... I do not need to overpower her. I just need to change the state of the matter.’
Aeliana didn’t fire her signature, hyper-compressed starlight beam.
She completely bypassed her standard, highly destructive offensive spellbook, digging deeply into the versatile, highly advanced arcane foundations of her Royal Elven heritage.
She ignored the freezing rain, ignored the terrifying roar of the beast, and focused entirely on the elemental composition of the battlefield.
’I will ensure that these girls survive!’
She slammed both of her pale trembling palms directly against the slick, rain-washed black stone of the elevated ridge she stood upon.
"Glacial Lock!" Aeliana shouted.
She forcefully injected a massive, highly concentrated surge of her entire remaining 1200 mana pool directly into the solid bedrock beneath her fingertips.
FWOOSH!
The temperature in the immediate vicinity of the swirling quicksand plummeted so violently and so suddenly that the heavy, falling sheets of rain instantly turned to jagged razor-sharp hail.
CRACK-CRACK-CRACK!
The hail bounced off the iron armor of the rookies as a blinding, pale-blue arcane geometric array violently expanded outward from Aeliana’s palms.
The intricate, glowing magical circle raced rapidly down the wet, jagged rocks and crashed directly into the swirling pressurized mud where the rookies were hopelessly trapped up to their waists.
The magical reaction was instantaneous and highly destructive to the environmental trap.
The frost magic violently clashed with the Matriarch’s earth manipulation.
Thick jagged glaciers of dark dense ice violently erupted across the churning surface of the quicksand.

The freezing magic aggressively consumed the slop as the blue light spider-webbed through the muddy water and instantly flash-freezed the swirling sucking vortex into a solid, highly uneven landscape of hard permafrost-level ice.
The five rookies gasped collectively, taking in huge, desperate lungfuls of the freezing air as the crushing pressure on their legs completely vanished.
The magical quicksand was entirely neutralized, leaving their heavy iron boots locked firmly and safely into the newly formed solid icy footholds.

"Pull your boots free! Climb the ice!" Aeliana commanded with her breath pluming thickly in the suddenly freezing air as the massive mana expenditure caused her pale hands to tremble violently against the black stone.𝒇𝓻𝓮𝓮𝙬𝙚𝒃𝒏𝓸𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝓬𝓸𝒎
She had drained her core to absolute zero to save them but the Mire-Drake Matriarch did not halt her terrifying assault.

Infuriated that her highly lethal, perfectly executed trap had been forcefully disabled by a mere fragile mortal standing on the rocks, the massive beast roared, entirely ignoring Silas on the high ground.
ROOOOOAAARRR!
’I really want to cut off your head...’

"Rowena, pull them out!" Silas ordered with his voice cracking like a whip.

He immediately stepped off the safety of the rocks and splashed heavily down into the shallows, his superheated mythril blade raised high, intending to draw the Matriarch’s attention before she could snap her jaws around the trapped girls.
"I can’t!" Rowena yelled back, her knuckles turning entirely white around her wooden staff with her face pale with absolute dread as she frantically calculated the magical physics.
"If I use a Gravity Well to pull them out of the quicksand, the multiplied gravitational pressure required to break the suction will instantly, violently crush their legs!"
The Matriarch let out a low, deeply satisfied rumble that vibrated through the dense mud, rattling the loose jagged black stones at the perilous edge of the flooded quarry.
RRRRRRRUMBLLLLLE!
It was a physical force that resonated in the chest cavities of the Vanguard, vibrating through the iron plates of their armor and rattling their teeth.
Seeing her prey hopelessly, perfectly pinned in the swirling vortex of her magical quicksand, the colossal beast coiled her massive armored crocodilian legs beneath her.
The thick, magically infused stone plates that acted as her natural armor scraped and ground against the submerged bedrock with a sickening scraping noise.

She prepared to launch her entire eighty-foot, siege-wagon-sized body directly across the span of the crater with her unhinged jaws ready to consume the five trapped, screaming girls in a single devastating blood-soaked bite.
Aeliana stared at the massive beast, her refined mind running complex arcane calculations in a fraction of a heartbeat.
She could feel the heavy density of the beast’s earth magic anchoring the slop, turning the natural terrain into a deadly pressurized weapon.

’The mud is actively pressurized by superior earth magic...’ Aeliana analyzed, her green eyes glowed with fierce determination as the freezing monsoon rain plastered her pristine silver hair directly to her pale cheeks. ’I cannot out-muscle a Tier 3 Boss’s elemental control since her raw output dwarfs mine by several orders of magnitude.
The density of her mana is simply too vast but...
I do not need to overpower her.
I just need to change the state of the matter.’
Aeliana didn’t fire her signature, hyper-compressed starlight beam.
She completely bypassed her standard, highly destructive offensive spellbook, digging deeply into the versatile, highly advanced arcane foundations of her Royal Elven heritage.
She ignored the freezing rain, ignored the terrifying roar of the beast, and focused entirely on the elemental composition of the battlefield.
’I will ensure that these girls survive!’
She slammed both of her pale trembling palms directly against the slick, rain-washed black stone of the elevated ridge she stood upon.
"Glacial Lock!" Aeliana shouted.
She forcefully injected a massive, highly concentrated surge of her entire remaining 1200 mana pool directly into the solid bedrock beneath her fingertips.
FWOOSH!
The temperature in the immediate vicinity of the swirling quicksand plummeted so violently and so suddenly that the heavy, falling sheets of rain instantly turned to jagged razor-sharp hail.
CRACK-CRACK-CRACK!
The hail bounced off the iron armor of the rookies as a blinding, pale-blue arcane geometric array violently expanded outward from Aeliana’s palms.
The intricate, glowing magical circle raced rapidly down the wet, jagged rocks and crashed directly into the swirling pressurized mud where the rookies were hopelessly trapped up to their waists.
The magical reaction was instantaneous and highly destructive to the environmental trap.
The frost magic violently clashed with the Matriarch’s earth manipulation.
Thick jagged glaciers of dark dense ice violently erupted across the churning surface of the quicksand.

The freezing magic aggressively consumed the slop as the blue light spider-webbed through the muddy water and instantly flash-freezed the swirling sucking vortex into a solid, highly uneven landscape of hard permafrost-level ice.
The five rookies gasped collectively, taking in huge, desperate lungfuls of the freezing air as the crushing pressure on their legs completely vanished.
The magical quicksand was entirely neutralized, leaving their heavy iron boots locked firmly and safely into the newly formed solid icy footholds.
"Pull your boots free!

Climb the ice!" Aeliana commanded with her breath pluming thickly in the suddenly freezing air as the massive mana expenditure caused her pale hands to tremble violently against the black stone.𝒇𝓻𝓮𝓮𝙬𝙚𝒃𝒏𝓸𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝓬𝓸𝒎
She had drained her core to absolute zero to save them but the Mire-Drake Matriarch did not halt her terrifying assault.

Infuriated that her highly lethal, perfectly executed trap had been forcefully disabled by a mere fragile mortal standing on the rocks, the massive beast roared, entirely ignoring Silas on the high ground.
ROOOOOAAARRR!
’I really want to cut off your head...’

chapters.title: Chapter 36: The War Is Over...
paragraphs: The massive corrupted crocodile launched herself entirely off the submerged rocks.

Her colossal armored body soared through the heavy rain, completely defying gravity for a terrifying moment as her cavernous jaws snapped wide open, revealing endless overlapping rows of jagged yellowed teeth aimed directly at the huddled struggling rookies who were frantically trying to chip their legs free from the dark ice.
Silas pushed his Mythic Gold Core to its highly volatile maximum.
A roaring brilliant golden aura erupted violently from his skin, completely vaporizing the rain around him into a thick cloud of hissing steam.
His muscles fired with terrifying superhuman velocity, drawing upon the deepest reserves of his sovereign foundation.

He surged forward off the elevated rocks, his boots shattering the jagged, dark ice beneath his feet with every thunderous step as he desperately tried to physically intercept the massive beast’s airborne trajectory.
CRASH! SHATTER! CRASH!
But the cold unforgiving reality of the battlefield crashed down on him with the weight of a collapsing mountain.
The physical distance was simply too great...

The quicksand trap had forcefully dragged the rookies nearly forty feet away from his starting position on the ridge, and the Matriarch’s armored, airborne momentum was simply too fast for even his enhanced physique to match since he wasn’t that high leveled...
He was going to be more than two seconds too late to block the devastating bone-crushing bite.
’Dammit,’ Silas thought with his grip tightening around the heavy hilt of his mythril blade until the leather groaned.
He gritted his teeth, fully preparing to watch these girls suffer their very first casualties under his direct command.
He could heal them yes... but...
’Wait Eluned...!’ He glanced at the Watchtower in the distance... He was not fighting this war alone.
He had built a territory, and that territory was watching his back.
High above the flooded, treacherous, slop-filled quarry, the bruising, dark-purple clouds of the raging monsoon violently tore open.
WHOOOSHHHHHH!

The deafening roar of the rain and the terrifying snarling of the descending Matriarch were entirely overpowered by an incredibly high-pitched shriek of hyper-compressed mana violently tearing its way through the dense atmosphere.
SCREEEEEEECH!
Miles away, standing safely atop the massive, seventy-foot, rune-carved observation deck of the towering Blood-Iron Watchtower, the situation was entirely under flawless control.
"Phew..." Eluned sighed, using this thing was fun!
Eluned and Fenna had not taken their eyes off the magically-assisted ballista scopes for a single second since the ground teams had deployed.
The SSS-Rank Goddess and the Bow-Splitter captain had actively, meticulously tracked the massive spike in Silas’s Gold Core mana, recognizing the signs of an escalating engagement.

Through the glowing blue reticles of the heavy artillery, they watched the massive, highly armored signature of the Tier 3 Boss launch itself into the air toward the women’s vulnerable position on the ice.
The girls didn’t hesitate for a fraction of a heartbeat. They executed their overarching devastating heavy support role flawlessly.
KRA-THOOM! KRA-THOOM! KRA-THOOM!
The heavy Abyssal-Marrow-cooled ballistae fired in rapid, utterly deafening succession.
The massive bowstrings, forged from the sinews of the cold blood, snapped forward with enough force to shatter a castle wall.
Three colossal, hyper-compressed bolts of blinding, pure blue mana screamed down from the heavens.

The artillery strikes moved with devastating velocity, trailing massive, spiraling vacuums of displaced air that violently pushed the heavy rain clouds aside, leaving three perfectly clear, smoking holes in the gray sky.
The rookies trapped on the ice screamed, covering their heads with their trembling arms as the gray sky directly above them literally ignited with blinding blue light.

The orbital strikes were flawlessly calculated, utilizing the Watchtower’s Tier 2 targeting enchantments and Fenna as well as Eluned’s peerless sniper aim to perfectly track the massive airborne trajectory of the Mire-Drake Matriarch.
The first heavy, mythril-tipped ballista bolt slammed directly into the Matriarch’s right shoulder while she was still fully suspended in the air with her jaws inches away from the nearest rookie.
KRA-CRACK!
The impact was apocalyptic.
The deafening concussive explosion violently arrested the massive beast’s forward momentum in mid-air.

The beast’s massive, deeply compressed plates of magically infused stone armor... which had evolved specifically to deflect physical blows utterly failed under the crushing weight of the siege weapon.
The thick stone plating shattered into a thousand jagged, lethal pieces of flying shrapnel that tore blindly through the rain, hissing as they struck the muddy water.
Before the beast’s primitive brain could even begin to register the agonizing pain of her shattered shoulder, the second bolt struck true.
BOOM!
The hyper-compressed blue mana slammed directly into the exact center of her heavily armored spine.

The resulting concussive shockwave was so massive and so incredibly dense, that it physically blew the falling monsoon rain completely backward, creating a brief unnatural shimmering dome of dry air over the center of the quarry.
Silas had placed himself between the girls and then spread out his mana covering them in it which stopped the force.
"Fuckkkkk...." Silas gritted his teeth as all the girls looked at his back, the immense wind pressure at their faces died down immediately as they were surrounded by the warm aura of their Lord.
’L-Lord Graves is so cool!’
The Matriarch’s massive spine violently buckled inward under the devastating impact.
The force drove her colossal, eighty-foot, multi-ton body straight down, altering her trajectory and slamming her violently toward the frozen mud instead of the huddled recruits.
The third and final bolt struck just as her soft unarmored belly hit the hard ice.
KRA-BOOM!
The final artillery strike buried itself deeply and ruthlessly into the massive exposed crater the previous two bolts had forcefully opened in her back.
The resulting explosion ripped violently, aggressively through the beast’s dense internal organs, blasting a highly destructive, smoking crater directly into the muddy earth beneath her.
SSPPPLLLLAAASSHH!
The explosive force sent a massive towering tidal wave of dark mud, shattered ice, and boiling water erupting in all directions, washing over the rocks and burning against Silas’s aura.
The Matriarch crashed heavily onto the frozen quicksand, her massive armored body twitching violently in agonizing spasms.
"UWAHHHHH!"
Black corrosive blood poured aggressively from the massive destructive, smoking wounds in her back.
The acidic blood pooled around her, rapidly melting the dark ice beneath her into a steaming foul-smelling puddle.
The five rookies slowly, shakily lowered their arms from their heads, staring up at the smoking, torn clouds and then down at the ruined, bleeding beast in complete shock.
They had just witnessed the terrifying might of the Blessed Land’s defensive siege capabilities.
They had literally been saved by the sky and their Lord too!
Silas dispelled his mana instantly and shot forward, he did not stop moving for a single second!
He knew a Tier 3 Boss was incredibly resilient, possessing a life force that made them practically immortal compared to the standard dispatched beasts of the basin.
Until the system interface explicitly confirmed the kill with a glowing blue tab, the beast was still an unpredictable threat that could easily snap a girl in half with a final death spasm.
’I’ll kill it once and for all!’
Silas didn’t waste the devastating opening his Watchtower had just flawlessly provided.

He utilized his terrifying forward momentum as he planted his heavy boot directly onto a massive protruding pillar of Aeliana’s dark ice, using the solid, unyielding structure as a highly stable springboard.
CRUNCH-SHATTER!
The thick ice violently shattered into a thousand glittering, pale shards under the massive force of his leg muscles as he launched himself incredibly high into the rain-soaked air.
Silas soared gracefully, directly over the twitching crippled body of the massive Matriarch.
"Burn..." Silas commanded coldly as he channeled every single remaining drop of his roaring Mythic Gold Core directly down his muscular arms and into the heavy hilt of his weapon.
The Umbral-Forged Mythril Blade responded violently to its master’s call.
The dark-purple veins running through the metal instantly ignited, glowing with a terrifying golden heat that rivaled the energy coming out of Silas’s own core.
The freezing rain hissed aggressively, instantly turning to white steam the exact fraction of a second it struck the superheated metal.
Silas flawlessly twisted his muscular torso in mid-air, utilizing the falling momentum of his entire body to maximize the output of the strike.
’I only have one strike so I have to make it count...’

He brought the glowing golden blade down in a devastating brutal plunge, aiming precisely for the smoking bleeding wound the orbital strikes had ripped open at the very base of the Matriarch’s heavily armored skull.
The strike was perfect.
SHHHHK!
The superheated mythril blade met exactly zero resistance. It effortlessly, flawlessly cleaved through the ruined fragments of the stone plating.
It sank deeply into the dense mutated musculature of the beast’s heavy neck.

The radiant heat of the Gold Core aggressively cauterized the massive wound as the blade passed through the flesh, literally cooking the meat from the inside out and burning away the highly corrosive black blood before it could even attempt to splash onto Silas’s pristine armor.
"CREEEEEEE!"
With a sickening bone-shattering crunch that echoed sharply across the silent quarry, the dark blade completely and permanently severed the thick bundle of nerves comprising the beast’s spinal cord.
The Mire-Drake Matriarch rigidly, violently locked up. Every single muscle in her massive body pulled taut in a final, agonizing reflex.
CLACK!
Her massive jaws snapped shut with a deafening sound that shook the remaining shards of ice.
Her four heavy, crocodilian, scale-covered legs violently kicked out against the mud one final, desperate time, sending a massive arching spray of brown slop high into the rainy air.
Then, the colossal, eighty-foot, siege-wagon-sized beast went entirely limp.
The sickly, corrupted life faded rapidly from her glowing yellow reptilian eyes, and she collapsed onto the frozen mud, becoming nothing more than a towering mountain of defeated smoking flesh.
BOOM!

The flooded quarry violently shook one last time as the massive weight finally settled completely displacing gallons of muddy water and then, the environment rapidly descended into a dead suffocating silence, broken only by the relentless drumming of the monsoon rain against the dark armor of the girls.
Pitter-patter! Pitter-patter!
Silas landed atop the beast’s massive scaly back.

His boots easily found purchase between the shattered bloody stone plates as he kept his grip firmly, tightly wrapped around the hilt of his deeply embedded sword, refusing to let go until he was certain.

His broad chest heaved slightly with his breath pluming in the cold air as the blazing radiant golden aura slowly retracted back into his internal spiritual pathways, leaving him standing in the gloom.
He waited for the undeniable confirmation from the sovereign laws of the world.
A moment later, a massive glowing holographic blue tab violently materialized directly in the exact center of his vision, illuminating the rain.
[Target Eliminated: Mire-Drake Matriarch (Tier 3 Boss)]
[Assist Recorded: Watchtower Ballista Array]
[Lord Silas has slain a Tier 3 Boss! +30 UP]
[You have leveled up! You have leveled up!]
A massive surge of pure energy flooded violently into his system.
The level-up forced his internal mana pathways to violently expand, searing through his veins like liquid fire.
It forcibly knitted his muscle fibers tighter, radically increasing his bone density and total physical output.
The dull exhaustion of the explosive sprint entirely vanished, completely replaced by the intoxicating addictive thrill of ascension.
’I love leveling up...’
He felt stronger, faster, and infinitely more lethal.
"Haah..."
Silas exhaled a long breath, finally relaxing his grip.
He grabbed the hilt of his weapon with both hands and pulled his mythril blade free from the beast’s severed neck with a wet satisfying squelch.
He looked down from the high ground of the corpse at the five rookies.
They were still huddled on the ice, shivering from the cold, staring up at him as if he were a literal god of war descended from the heavens to deliver them from the jaws of hell.
"Check your limbs," Silas commanded while smoothly returning his dark blade to its scabbard at his hip. "If anyone is bleeding, if anyone has suffered an acid burn or a twisted ankle, speak up now."
